entry.title: Spin-exchange-controlled nonclassical light in cavity electromagnetically induced transparency
entry.summary: Spin-Exchange-Controlled Nonclassical Light in Cavity Electromagnetically Induced Transparency arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a ring-cavity system with two three-level emitters coupled by a coherent spin-exchange interaction, using electromagnetically induced transparency to access a dark-state polariton. The authors show that strong photon antibunching appears when the one-polariton resonance nearly coincides with a destructive-interference minimum of the second-photon transition amplitude. By jointly tuning the exchange interaction and control-field strength, photon blockade with a finite intracavity population can be sustained over an extended range. The cavity-coupling phase is also shown to switch photon statistics between antibunching and bunching at fixed exchange strength.

entry.title: Measuring How Interactive Quantum Instruments Are
entry.summary: Operational Characterizations and Resource Structure of the Interactive Weight of Quantum Instruments arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces the interactive weight, a resource measure of how much of a quantum instrument cannot be explained by non-interactive components. Using tasks such as quantum-state recovery, positive linear loss games, and environment-assisted input-blind extraction, the authors give quantitative bounds and exact operational characterizations of this weight and its complement, the maximal non-interactive content. Within the allowed-operations framework of Hsieh et al., they establish resource-theoretic properties including faithfulness, convexity, and monotonicity.

entry.title: Learning effective entanglement Hamiltonians from observables
entry.summary: Observable-Based Learning of Effective Entanglement Hamiltonians arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes an observable-matching framework for learning effective entanglement Hamiltonians of interacting quantum many-body systems, demonstrated with response estimates from quantum Monte Carlo. The authors first calibrate the overall prefactor of the lattice Bisognano–Wichmann construction using equal-time correlations, then learn spatially resolved couplings without assuming a specific spatial form. Trained only on local correlations, the learned Hamiltonians reproduce benchmarked von Neumann and second Rényi entropies in 1D and second Rényi entropies in 2D.

entry.title: Fidelity Sets the Minimum Error of Quantum Recovery
entry.summary: Fidelity Determines the Minimum Error of Quantum Recovery arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies how quantum recovery operations can leave avoidable errors in later measurements, even when they maximize worst-input entanglement fidelity. It proves that for any finite-dimensional noise channel and fixed encoding, operational error and worst-input entanglement infidelity share the same minimum over all recovery operations. The authors also characterize optimal decoders and final corrections, including their sensitivity to residual unitary errors.

entry.title: Quantum simulation of classical RCL circuits via complexification and Schrödingerization
entry.summary: Quantum simulation of classical RCL circuits via complexification and Schrödingerization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper recalls the decomplexification procedure, which establishes a mathematical equivalence between finite-dimensional quantum dynamics and classical dynamics. It also discusses several strategies for complexifying classical equations to obtain corresponding quantum-equivalent dynamics. This allows solutions of classical differential equations to be prepared for implementation with quantum computing tools.

entry.title: Linking coherence, concurrence and Bell correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: Unifying First-Order Coherence, Concurrence, and Bell Correlations in Three-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies exact relations among first-order coherence, pairwise concurrence and the maximal CHSH value in coherent three-flavor neutrino oscillations. The evolving neutrino is modeled as a three-qubit single-excitation state, from which the two-qubit reduced states are derived. The authors show that the squared first-order coherence of each flavor and its two squared concurrences sum to one, and that the maximal CHSH value follows a two-branch relation fixed by average coherence and concurrence.

entry.title: Bounds on few-copy Gaussian state tomography and the lack of a fermionic warm regime
entry.summary: Upper and lower bounds for few-copy Gaussian tomography, and the absence of a fermionic warm regime arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how many copies of a Gaussian quantum state are needed for tomography when only a few copies can be measured together. It proves that adaptive single-copy tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states requires Ω(m³/ε²) copies, and extends this bound to blocks of up to k copies. The paper also shows that fermionic systems lack the warm regime found for bosonic systems, and gives matching upper bounds for several classes of states.

entry.title: Thermally-driven quantum reservoir computing: a quantum computing approach that encodes input data in the temperature of a heat bath
entry.summary: Thermally-driven quantum reservoir computing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes a quantum reservoir computing paradigm in which input data is encoded in the time-dependent temperature of a thermal bath, using the fading memory produced by energy dissipation. The authors derive an exact expression for the nonlinear response of any fixed readout and prove a memory-nonlinearity trade-off that is structural rather than tunable. They illustrate the results with a driven qubit and a pair of coupled qubits, concluding that observable choice and bath engineering are the main physical levers.

entry.title: Geometry optimization for detecting gravity-induced entanglement in matter-wave interferometers
entry.summary: Improving Gravitationally Induced Entanglement in Interferometric Configurations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how to detect entanglement between massive particles caused by gravity, using Stern-Gerlach and Mach-Zehnder matter-wave interferometers. The authors derive exact analytical expressions for the gravitational phase of each configuration and compare several geometric orientations. They find that geometric optimization is essential, with parallel-arms designs giving the largest phase accumulation and greater robustness. Some symmetric Mach-Zehnder setups show destructive-interference nulls where detection fails.

entry.title: Nonequilibrium spin-glass order in a long-range quantum Ising glass and its noise sensitivity
entry.summary: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies spin-glass order in a long-range quantum Ising glass after a transverse-field quench. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order matches at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, while in between, cold shells exceed it and hot shells fall below it. The authors attribute this to a competition in correlation space between the rigidity of populated eigenstates and the spread of their pair patterns. Under weak longitudinal dephasing, the zero-field endpoint stays exactly fixed while the finite-quench response weakens, offering a self-referenced noise probe for quantum spin simulators.

entry.title: Aligning measurements with magnetic flux surfaces to overcome anisotropy limits in quantum subspace heat-conduction solvers
entry.summary: Field-aligned measurement removes the anisotropy barrier of sample-based quantum subspace solvers for magnetized-plasma heat conduction arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies heat conduction in magnetized plasmas, where thermal anisotropy can reach 10^8 to 10^10. The authors use sample-based quantum subspace methods and prove that when the measurement basis is aligned with flux surfaces, the error decreases as anisotropy grows. In a computational basis, missing a single node on a flux surface causes an error floor. Tests on a ten-qubit superconducting processor show the aligned basis yields much lower errors than the computational basis.

entry.title: Correcting particle loss using quantum states with $2^l$-photon steps
entry.summary: Particle-loss error correction using 2^l-step states generated via particle-number-resolving measurement schemes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents an iterative scheme for generating finite superpositions of Fock states whose photon numbers differ by $2^l$. It derives an upper bound on the probability of generating such states. Several bosonic encodings built on this class of states are constructed and compared for correcting particle-loss errors. The most efficient encoding achieves a higher channel fidelity than previously studied bosonic encodings.

entry.title: Review of Quantum Noise Engineering in Advanced LIGO
entry.summary: Quantum Noise Engineering in Advanced LIGO arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This review examines quantum noise in Advanced LIGO, a gravitational-wave detector. It explains how vacuum fluctuations entering the readout port cause measurement imprecision and radiation-pressure back-action through quadrature descriptions. The paper follows squeezed vacuum from generation through the filter cavity and interferometer to readout. It discusses how frequency-independent and frequency-dependent squeezing shape quantum noise.

entry.title: Detector response to vacuum fluctuations inside a shell of delocalized mass
entry.summary: Unruh-DeWitt detectors in a delocalized massive shell arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper models how a detector responds to vacuum fluctuations inside a hollow massive shell that is in a superposition of positions. The delocalized source mass creates a superposition of spacetime geometries and their vacuum fluctuations. The authors use quantum reference frames to analyze the detector dynamics on a definite curved spacetime. They show that, under appropriate postselection, the detector's response function displays interference patterns.

entry.title: Coherent detector responses in quantum-controlled spherical-shell geometries
entry.summary: Coherent detector responses to quantum-controlled spherical-shell geometries arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper constructs the response of a compactly switched Unruh-DeWitt detector on a quantum-controlled pair of transparent spherical-shell spacetimes sharing the same ADM mass. A stipulated common incoming scattering identification places both branch excitations in one Hilbert space, and their Gram matrix determines joint, conditional, and dephased detector responses. For concentric shells the centered response is exactly s-wave, and the equal-radius benchmark shows conditional changes of about 25%. These are relational, model-dependent detector responses rather than background-independent evidence of quantum geometry.

entry.title: Chiral giant atom in ultrastrong waveguide QED: ground-state dressing and delayed feedback
entry.summary: Ground-State Dressing and Delayed Feedback of a Chiral Giant Atom in Ultrastrong Waveguide QED arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a chiral giant atom ultrastrongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two separated points. At a relative coupling phase of π/2, the total spectral density does not depend on the distance between the coupling points, while its directional components do. Using a variational polaron transformation, the authors show that the renormalized transition frequency and total ground-state dressing share this independence, while the virtual-photon cloud remains chiral.

entry.title: Detecting a type of exotic quantum phase in 2D systems using a new efficient method
entry.summary: Agnostic and efficient detection of ℤ₂ symmetry-protected topological phases in projected entangled-pair states arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents a method for detecting interacting Z₂ two-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases from the ground state represented as an infinite projected entangled-pair state. The approach does not depend on the symmetry representation in the virtual space or on the bond dimension, and it works directly in the thermodynamic limit without finite-size scaling. The authors numerically map phase boundaries away from fixed-point wavefunctions and extract the SPT label cocycle data explicitly from the PEPS tensor.

entry.title: A single-cycle method to prepare ground states using strongly coupled baths
entry.summary: Single-shot ground-state preparation via strongly coupled baths arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes cooling protocols that operate at strong coupling between a quantum many-body system and its bath, showing that accurate ground states can be reached in even a single cooling cycle. The protocols combine dynamically ramped ancilla energy levels with time-dependent couplings to balance cooling error against physical time. For free-fermion systems, the dynamics is reduced exactly to a two-level scattering problem, leading to a family of "Möbius-Ingham" protocols. The authors also test the approach on interacting Ising and t-V chains and the two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model, and extend it to Gibbs state preparation for free fermions.

entry.title: Threshold-free quantum memory using symmetry-enriched topological codes
entry.summary: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies whether non-Abelian symmetry enrichment can protect a toric code quantum memory against incoherent electric noise at any bond error probability. For a honeycomb-lattice toric code coupled to Sp(N) rotors, the authors build an efficient minimum-weight decoder whose logical error probability decays exponentially with system size when N is at least 40. The same decoder rules out strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in the fundamental channel of Sp(N) under corresponding local decoherence in two dimensions. The construction extends to other symmetries, including SU(N).

entry.title: Constraint variance identity and matter-geometry fluctuation relation
entry.summary: Constraint Variance Identity and the Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the quantum Hamiltonian constraint in quantum gravity, which vanishes for physical states. For separable minisuperspace Hamiltonians, the vanishing of its variance yields a fundamental identity. Under the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, the authors derive a Matter-Geometry Fluctuation Relation linking spacetime clock fluctuations to matter fluctuations, along with a quantitative stability condition for the clock against total quantum noise and an uncertainty relation between matter energy and relational time.

entry.title: Thesis on how quantum entanglement changes over time in holographic theories
entry.summary: On Entanglement Dynamics in Holographic Theories arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This thesis uses the AdS/CFT correspondence to study how entanglement entropy evolves in time in strongly coupled quantum field theories. It examines an exactly solvable two-dimensional conformal field theory with a sine-square deformation and compares the results with holographic calculations. It also develops entanglement membrane descriptions for chaotic many-body systems and reflected entropy, and uses them to study the time evolution of multipartite entanglement.

entry.title: Nonlocal magic of fermions bounded by entanglement fluctuations, logarithmic for free fermions
entry.summary: Nonlocal magic of fermions is bounded by entanglement fluctuations and is logarithmic for free fermions arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies nonlocal magic, a quantum resource that cannot be removed by local unitaries, in free-fermion states. It shows that local Gaussian unitaries minimize nonlocal stabilizer Rényi entropy only up to three fermion pairs, not from four pairs on. General local non-Gaussian unitaries that preserve fermion parity map m free-fermion pairs to fermionic Bell pairs with fidelity decaying at most as 1/√m, so nonlocal magic grows logarithmically rather than linearly in m. This bound is governed by the capacity of entanglement, which grows only linearly for free-fermion pairs.

entry.title: Multipartite entanglement and TQFT partition functions via PL bordism
entry.summary: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper examines whether multi-invariants of a gapped system's ground state can isolate the partition functions of a topological quantum field theory. The answer is governed by oriented bordism: for null-bordant manifolds the partition function is extractable from a finite family of invariants. In dimension four the obstruction is the signature, so extraction is possible only when the signature vanishes, while torsion invariants are not obstructed.

entry.title: Every Bell inequality with quantum advantage in the minimal scenario is self-testing
entry.summary: All Bell inequalities with a quantum advantage in the minimal scenario are self-testing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies which correlations maximize a given Tsirelson inequality in the minimal Bell scenario, and which inequalities a given correlation maximizes. It shows that every Tsirelson inequality with quantum advantage is maximized by a single extremal correlation, which self-tests the corresponding realization. The authors also show that at most a two-dimensional family of inequalities can be maximized by a nonlocal extremal correlation, and conclude that the quantum set is not self-dual.

entry.title: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Quantum-Dot Devices
entry.summary: FNO-Based Inverse Co-Design of Semiconducting Quantum-Dot Devices arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a differentiable inverse co-design framework for electrostatically defined semiconductor quantum dots that jointly optimises gate voltages and gate electrode layout. A Fourier neural operator surrogate, trained on data from a semiclassical Thomas-Fermi simulator, predicts two-dimensional charge-density fields with a relative L2 test error of 0.6%. The surrogate evaluates a single design about 17,000 times faster on GPU than the CPU-based physics simulator. In a gradient-based loop with fabrication constraints, the method produces both vertically and horizontally elongated double-dot confinement geometries from the same initial conditions.

entry.title: Physical conditions for quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation
entry.summary: Physical regimes of quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines the physical conditions under which quantum algorithms for elastic media simulation could achieve a quartic quantum advantage over classical methods. For continuum elastic dynamics at fixed volume with spatial convergence order m, it finds an end-to-end speedup of about (m+4)/(m+1) in simulation time and 4/(m+1) in accuracy, with an exponential memory advantage. The authors also define microscopically resolved bulk observables (MRBOs) and propose pseudorandom heterogeneous materials as an explicit application where their estimation may show a quartic quantum advantage.

entry.title: Frustration-freeness can be decided but not proven
entry.summary: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the frustration-free property of quantum many-body systems, where ground states minimize all local interaction terms simultaneously. For a fixed local Hilbert space dimension, the authors show a Hamiltonian-independent finite system-size cutoff exists, so checking frustration-freeness at that size decides it for all sizes. They also show some frustration-free Hamiltonians have frustration-freeness unprovable in ZFC. The two results are reconciled because the cutoff, though finite for each dimension, is uncomputable as a function of that dimension.

entry.title: Quantum one-way and SMP communication gains for total functions
entry.summary: Asymptotic advantage of quantum one-way and SMP communication for total functions arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper constructs a total Boolean function on n input bits. Its bounded-error quantum simultaneous-message (SMP) communication complexity, and hence its quantum one-way complexity, is O(√n), while its randomised one-way complexity is Ω(n). The authors also show that, when the players share O(√n) EPR pairs, the same function has a classical SMP protocol of cost O(√n).

entry.title: Scalable transpilation method for overcoming connectivity limits in distributed superconducting quantum architectures
entry.summary: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a scalable transpilation method for distributed superconducting quantum architectures with restricted inter- and intra-module connectivity. It combines a graph-partitioning mapping step with a fast SABRE-inspired routing heuristic, called the quantum interaction graph approach. On a 48-qubit architecture, the method reports over 250 times speed-ups for structured workloads compared with the DMapS algorithm and cost reductions of up to about 24%. It also maintains practical runtimes on the 399-qubit IBM Flamingo, where DMapS times out on dense circuits.

entry.title: Dithered Belief Propagation for Real-Time Quantum Memory Decoding
entry.summary: Dithered Belief Propagation for Real-Time Quantum Memory Decoding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a dithered belief-propagation (BP) decoder for circuit-level quantum memory, aiming to reduce the oscillations and trapping that limit standard BP decoders for qLDPC codes. The method combines a quantum-adapted sign-flip mechanism with chained randomized prior perturbation. Under circuit-level noise, it is evaluated on the distance-11 rotated surface code and the distance-12 bivariate-bicycle code, where it significantly outperforms BP and BP+OSD+CS-10. It matches or exceeds Relay-BP accuracy, especially at higher physical error rates, while cutting multiplications by about 98% on average and eliminating node-level RNGs.

entry.title: A tensor-network Chebyshev–Galerkin method for solving boundary-value problems in mechanics
entry.summary: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a quantum-inspired numerical method that represents fields and operators as quantics tensor trains (QTT) and assembles and solves global spectral systems directly in compressed form. It handles coupled elliptic systems with variable coefficients, mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet–Robin boundary conditions. Parameters and random inputs are treated as extra coordinates, so one solve yields solutions across a whole parameter space. The authors report errors below 10^-8 on a three-dimensional linear elasticity benchmark, along with a six-parameter cantilever design study and memory savings for a stochastic problem.

entry.title: Speeding up exchange calculations in quantum chemistry on multi-core CPUs with SIMD instructions
entry.summary: Vectorized and Symbolically Optimized Seminumerical Exchange for Large-Scale Quantum Chemistry arXiv · Oct 15, 2026This paper presents SNK, a seminumerical exchange algorithm based on the sn-LinK method, optimized for modern multi-core CPUs with SIMD vector instructions and implemented in the Q-Chem program. The authors describe vectorization and memory strategies for Boys function and three-center one-electron integral kernels, generated symbolically with SymPy and exported as optimized C++ code. Tests on systems of 100-500 atoms and 2000-10000 basis functions show 1-2 orders of magnitude speedups over traditional four-center exchange. For smaller molecules, SNK surpasses occ-RI-K beyond roughly 50-100 atoms.

entry.title: Can the Quantum Fisher Effective Dimension Judge a Hybrid Quantum Neural Network?
entry.summary: What Does the Effective Dimension of a Hybrid Quantum Neural Network Actually Measure? arXiv · Oct 8, 2026This paper examines what the effective dimension of a quantum Fisher information matrix actually measures in hybrid quantum neural networks. The authors test it across two image datasets, four frozen backbones including a random-projection control, four circuit depths on eight qubits, and three seeds. Its correlation with test accuracy varies widely in sign and size, and it is nearly identical across backbones, so the authors conclude it reflects circuit geometry rather than model quality.

entry.title: Optimal Quantum Junta Testing Without Inverse Queries
entry.summary: Optimal Quantum Junta Testing arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper studies how many queries are needed to test whether an unknown n-qubit unitary or quantum channel acts nontrivially on at most k qubits. The authors consider a forward-only query model without inverse or controlled access, and prove tight bounds of Θ(k/(ε²log k)) for a broad range of ε. For channels, this closes the gap between earlier upper and lower bounds at constant ε. The results rely on a connection between quantum junta testing and classical support-size testing. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show that forward-only quantum junta testing needs Θ(k/(ε²log k)) queries for large k, linking it to classical support-size testing with tight bounds, and contrast this with Õ(√k) queries

entry.title: Fermionic analogue of the Porter-Thomas distribution and how it arises in random matchgate circuits
entry.summary: Fermionic Porter-Thomas statistics and their emergence in random matchgate circuits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper derives the measurement-probability distribution for random fermionic Gaussian states, with and without particle-number conservation, which is the fermionic counterpart of the Porter-Thomas law. For large systems the probabilities become log-normally distributed with moments growing polynomially in system size. The authors also show how this distribution emerges in random one-dimensional brickwork matchgate circuits and prove depth requirements for the collision probability to converge. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive an exact Porter-Thomas analogue for random fermionic Gaussian states, show it emerges in matchgate circuits, and report a proof that collision probability requires depth growing alm

entry.title: Using topology to classify all mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions
entry.summary: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies mutually unbiased bases (MUBs), which are complementary quantum measurements in which certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. Using the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, the authors classify all sets of MUBs in dimension six. They show that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix, which implies that no four MUBs exist. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use topological connectedness to classify all mutually unbiased triples in dimension six and report that no fourth basis exists.

entry.title: Efficient quantum ultraspherical transform and a well-conditioned quantum spectral method: a transform and spectral solver for solving linear differential equations on quantum computers.
entry.summary: Efficient quantum ultraspherical transform and a well-conditioned quantum spectral method arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper constructs a quantum ultraspherical transform (QUT) for orthonormal ultraspherical polynomials, converting between amplitudes of function values and expansion coefficients. For each fixed integer m≥2 and dimensions with N+m=2^n, the transform achieves error at most ε with a gate count polynomial in n and log(1/ε), built on the quantum Fourier transform. Using the QUT, the authors develop a quantum spectral solver for regular linear ordinary differential equations, where preconditioning keeps condition numbers bounded independently of basis size under suitable assumptions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct a quantum ultraspherical transform for all integer m≥2 and a spectral solver for linear ODEs with bounded preconditioned condition numbers.

entry.title: Discovering correlated error mechanisms: data-driven augmentation of detector error models to improve decoding
entry.summary: Discovering correlated error mechanisms: data-driven augmentation of detector error models improving decoding arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a data-driven method that discovers new error mechanisms directly from experimental detector-firing statistics to augment detector error models (DEMs) for quantum error correction. Candidates are built by combining pairs of existing mechanisms and then filtered using pairwise and higher-order detector correlations. In surface-code simulations with correlated noise, the augmented model raised the Lambda parameter by 20% and cut the logical error rate by 75% at code distance 15. On Google superconducting device data, it raised Lambda by 9% and reduced the logical error rate by 14% at distance 7. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report discovering new correlated error mechanisms from experimental detector statistics with assigned logical effects, validated on surface-code simulations and Google superconducting dat

entry.title: Compatibility of Pauli Observables: A study of whether one measurement can approximate several Pauli observables
entry.summary: Compatibility of Pauli Observables arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how sharply a single measurement can approximate an arbitrary finite family of Pauli observables, and what sharpness tradeoffs result. The authors derive an exact state-space correspondence linking incompatibility to preparation uncertainty, and they construct explicit parent measurements via Pauli conjugation and classical randomisation. The paper also shows that magic is necessary to reach the full compatibility region of every noncommuting Pauli family. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a state-space correspondence characterising Pauli compatibility regions, linking incompatibility to preparation uncertainty and showing magic is necessary, with exact results reported

entry.title: Equivalence of correlated catalytic and marginal asymptotic transformations in quantum resource theories
entry.summary: Equivalence of Correlated Catalytic and Marginal Asymptotic Transformations in Quantum Resource Theories arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proves that correlated-catalytic state conversion is possible exactly when the marginal asymptotic conversion rate is at least one. The equivalence holds for arbitrary states across broad classes of entanglement, coherence, and magic theories. Under local operations and classical communication, the authors fully characterize conversion from arbitrary bipartite states to entangled pure states via distillable entanglement. They show that correlated catalysts cannot increase distillable entanglement or distillable secret key, nor make bound entanglement distillable. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove correlated-catalytic conversion is equivalent to marginal asymptotic rate at least one, extending to distillable entanglement and secret key results.

entry.title: Whether energy gaps of quantum matter survive weak local perturbations, given only locality and translation invariance
entry.summary: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the stability of energy gaps in macroscopic quantum many-body systems, assuming only locality and translation invariance. The authors show that in any spatial dimension there exist gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state whose gap becomes unstable, closing under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbations in the thermodynamic limit. For one-dimensional spin and fermionic systems, such unstable-gap Hamiltonians must break translation invariance and be fine-tuned. In dimensions greater than one, fine-tuned translation-invariant local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and unstable gap are shown to exist. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show existence of gapped local Hamiltonians with unique ground state but unstable gap in any dimension, with one-dimensional characterizations.

entry.title: Shadow bootstrapping: pure-state tomography with few measurement settings
entry.summary: Shadow bootstrapping: Nearly minimal-setting pure-state tomography with shallow Clifford measurements arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a method for reconstructing unknown pure quantum states using nearly the fewest possible measurement settings. The algorithm uses single-copy, nonadaptive shallow Clifford measurements, each implemented by a circuit of depth O(log n), and achieves optimal sample complexity. Its key technique, shadow bootstrapping, uses the current estimate to reduce the variance of later residual estimates. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose shadow bootstrapping, achieving near-minimal measurement settings and optimal sample complexity for pure-state tomography with shallow Clifford measurements.

entry.title: Operator-norm bounds on sums of positive operators, with applications to quantum games and key distribution
entry.summary: Norm Bounds on Sums of Positive Operators with Applications to Monogamy Games and Quantum Key Distribution arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proves a general inequality bounding the operator norm of averages of positive semidefinite operators, which can be used to bound quantum measurement acceptance probabilities. It applies this to the parallel BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement game, identifying the robustness threshold at which the optimal winning probability decays exponentially or stays bounded away from zero. It also shows that one-sided device-independent BB84 quantum key distribution achieves any asymptotic key rate below 1 minus 2 times the binary entropy of the tolerated bit-error rate. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a general operator-norm inequality for sums of positive operators and apply it to sharp thresholds in parallel BB84 monogamy games and one-sided device-independent QKD rates.

entry.title: Algorithmic wave-particle duality: finding paths in welded trees is hard
entry.summary: Algorithmic Wave-Particle Duality: Pathfinding in Welded Trees is Hard arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the welded trees problem, in which an algorithm must navigate a randomly labeled graph made of two binary trees joined at their leaves, from one root to the other. Quantum walks can do this exponentially faster than any classical method, but recording the path destroys the interference behind that speedup. The authors prove that, for trees of height n, finding a root-to-root path with constant probability requires quantum query complexity Θ̃(2^{n/3}), and that this bound is tight. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a tight quantum query bound of 2^(n/3) for finding root-to-root paths in welded trees, using the compressed permutation oracle.

entry.title: Lower Bounds for Quantum Estimation With Persistent Memory
entry.summary: Structural Lower Bounds for Quantum Property Estimation with Persistent Memory arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies quantum property estimation, where an experimenter estimates expectation values of a family of observables from independent copies of an unknown state to additive error ε. The authors develop a backward-induction framework based on operator resolvents, reducing the lower bound to an algebraic certificate computed from the target observables with Ω(1/ε²) scaling. For a persistent memory of dimension K, they show lower bounds that match memoryless or commuting estimators within polylogarithmic factors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a resolvent-based backward induction reducing persistent-memory lower bounds to algebraic certificates, with tight bounds for Pauli and Majorana estimation.

entry.title: Learning quantum dynamics despite unknown state preparation and measurement errors
entry.summary: SPAM-robust learnability of quantum dynamics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies which properties of quantum dynamics can still be learned when state preparation and measurement (SPAM) errors are unknown. It treats quantum channels and continuous-time evolution in one framework, using the cycle structure of a generalized pattern-transfer graph to characterize all learnable parameter combinations and building explicit SPAM-robust learning protocols. It also shows that coherent structure greatly restricts gauge ambiguity, making coherent coefficients and broad classes of dissipative error parameters individually learnable. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize learnable parameters via cycle structure of a generalized pattern-transfer graph, and show coherent structure reduces continuous gauge freedom to discrete or trivial choices.

entry.title: Linear-time recovery of erased bits in quantum expander codes
entry.summary: Linear-time erasure recovery for quantum expander codes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces Small-Set-Peeling, a quantum generalization of the classical Peeling decoder for erasure errors in quantum expander codes. The decoder can correct up to D−1 erasures, where D is the design distance of the code, and it is guaranteed to run in linear time. Combined with the erasure-conversion algorithm Small-Set-Find, the authors also obtain a graph-local linear-time decoder for Pauli errors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors generalize the classical Peeling decoder to quantum expander codes, reporting the first guaranteed linear-time correction of D-1 erasures, combined with erasure conversion for Pauli errors

entry.title: A quantum lower bound for finding triangles in graphs
entry.summary: A Quantum Lower Bound for Triangle Finding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies triangle finding, a basic graph problem where the input is an N-vertex graph given by its adjacency matrix. The best known quantum query upper bound was O(N^{5/4}), while the best lower bound was the basic Ω(N) from unstructured search. The authors prove that Ω(N^{13/12}) quantum queries are necessary, the first superlinear quantum query lower bound for this problem. The same bound also holds for triangle detection and for detecting any fixed connected non-bipartite graph. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first superlinear quantum query lower bound Ω(N^{13/12}) for triangle finding, using compressed oracles and transfer methods.

entry.title: Faster Exact and Approximate Quantum Fourier Transforms Built on Multiplication
entry.summary: Improved Exact and Approximate Quantum Fourier Transforms from Multiplication arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The quantum Fourier transform is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, including Shor's factoring algorithm and phase estimation. The paper reduces the gate count of exact QFT circuits to O(q log q), improving on earlier bounds. It also shows that a multiplication circuit with O(n(log n)^α) gates yields a QFT circuit with O(q(log q)^α) gates. For approximate QFT, the paper further improves the gate count bound. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give improved gate-count bounds for exact and approximate QFT by transferring multiplication circuit complexity to QFT circuits.

entry.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Approximating Energy in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Spin Glass Model
entry.summary: A Fully Polynomial Approximation Algorithm for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses approximating the maximum energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass model. It introduces GEG-IAMP, an algorithm whose total work is polynomial in both the dimension N and the inverse accuracy 1/ε, with a finite-size probabilistic guarantee. The method replaces the Onsager correction with Reeves's coupling construction and groups Euler-Maruyama steps into O(1/ε) matrix-vector products. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first SK maximum-energy approximation with work polynomial in both N and 1/ε, plus a finite-size guarantee.

entry.title: Exact Resource Depth for Single-Qubit Dyadic Quantum Programs
entry.summary: Arithmetic Depth, Minimal Gate Alphabets, and Exact Program-State Resources for Single-Qubit Dyadic Programs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a single-qubit dyadic fragment of quantum programs, where the deepest exact resource layer can be determined exactly rather than bounded. The authors prove a descent theorem for a projective Clifford-cyclotomic tower and combine it with an arithmetic-closure invariant for adaptive stabilizer processing. They show that three depth measures coincide: the minimal real cyclotomic field, the shallowest gate alphabet, and the shallowest program-state layer. The result is packaged as an exact static resource effect with an outlined certificate-producing compiler.

entry.title: A 3D-printed one-piece optical mount base for an unbalanced interferometer
entry.summary: 3D Printed Monolithic Optomechanical Chassis for an Unbalanced Field-Widened Interferometer arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a single-piece optomechanical base built with laser powder bed fusion, a metal 3D printing method, from Invar36, a low-thermal-expansion alloy. Optical mounts, flexures, and alignment features are built directly into the base, which the authors say produces a smaller footprint than conventional assemblies. The authors suggest the approach could support lightweight, customized optical systems and next-generation quantum sensors.

entry.title: Testing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors
entry.summary: Probing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes a near-field experiment in which a levitated microrotor modulates a mass quadrupole and a second rotor measures the resulting gravitational tidal field as a torque, reaching megahertz frequencies. At 2 MHz the estimated torque is 2×10⁻²⁵ Nm. The authors argue this could constrain any delay in gravitational coupling to the 10⁻⁸ s level, more than three orders of magnitude better than existing bounds.

entry.title: Optimal Holding Times for Entanglement Swapping: tuning how long quantum entanglement is stored to maximize swap throughput
entry.summary: Optimal Holding Times for Entanglement Swapping arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how long entanglement should be held in memory-based quantum repeaters to maximize entanglement swapping throughput under strict, probabilistic, and mean fidelity constraints. It considers two heterogeneous quantum links that differ in decoherence rates, memory capacities, attempt rates, success probabilities, and classical communication latencies. The authors develop models to estimate expected throughput and the conditional wait-time distributions for swapping, then optimize the maximum holding times of both links to meet each fidelity requirement. The proposed model and approach are validated with a discrete-event quantum network simulator.

entry.title: Quantum algorithms for computing molecular response functions, compared across six routes with query lower bounds.
entry.summary: Quantum Algorithms for Molecular Response Functions: Resolvent Kernels, Time-Domain Sampling, Query Lower Bounds with Matched Single-Point Calibers, and a Six-Route Comparison arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper compares six quantum algorithm routes for molecular response functions within one resource-accounting framework, including resolvent-kernel and time-domain sampling approaches. It states conversions between the resource calibers of these routes and analyzes their error budgets and readout costs. It also proves query lower bounds for several tasks and presents an accounting map across the routes.

entry.title: Finite-temperature transition-window weights on a fault-tolerant quantum computer
entry.summary: Finite-temperature transition-window weights on a fault-tolerant quantum computer: duplex filtering on a thermal purification arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper extends the excite-filter-readout framework from zero-temperature pure ground states to Gibbs states, where filters act on absolute energies and thermal responses depend on transition frequencies. Using a Liouville-space and thermofield-double identity, it expresses the thermally weighted transition-window weight as a spectral projection and builds a routed block-encoding, a conjugate-pair readout, and a compatibility analysis of four routes. It gives a per-window query bound and reports that the preparation factor grows exponentially with system size at fixed temperature in positive-entropy-density systems.

entry.title: Resource-efficient ways to formulate the Knapsack problem for quantum computers
entry.summary: Resource-efficient formulations of the Knapsack problem for quantum computing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper examines how to express the Knapsack problem as a QUBO form that quantum computers can solve. It compares three resource-efficient formulations: a smaller penalty constant, fewer slack variables, and a method that avoids slack variables entirely. In simulations of the linear ramp QAOA and experiments on a D-Wave quantum annealer, all three approaches raised the chance of finding the optimal solution, with the slackless method performing best.

entry.title: Quantum entanglement between two particles colliding at non-relativistic speeds
entry.summary: Entanglement Entropy in Non Relativistic Collisions arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper numerically studies how entanglement entropy builds up between two non-relativistic particles that collide. The particles follow the ordinary Schrödinger equation with local, finite-range potentials, starting from the product of two independent wave packets. It examines several scenarios, including tunneling and mirror effects at low energy in front of a barrier, higher energies, and attraction instead of repulsion. Although the wave functions and density matrices differ significantly across these situations, the time trends and values of entanglement entropy look strikingly alike.

entry.title: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories with exact SL(2,R) gauge invariance
entry.summary: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories: 1D lattice models with exact rm SL(2,ℝ) gauge invariance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper revisits the Kogut-Susskind construction of gauge theories on a one-dimensional spatial lattice for the non-compact gauge group SL(2,R), keeping gauge invariance exact. Compared with compact groups, the Casimir operators of the gauge fields have a continuous spectrum and matter fields carry infinite-dimensional representations. For the pure gauge theory, restricting to the positive semigroup SL+(2,R) reproduces known results from the quantization of Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. The authors also add static charges and dynamical fermionic matter, obtaining an interacting one-dimensional SL(2,R) Kogut-Susskind gauge theory.

entry.title: Near-quantum-limited readout for an axion search using a sub-GHz amplifier
entry.summary: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain above 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. Measured with a variable-temperature noise source, its system noise is 2.5-3.5 quanta. The authors characterize performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, noise at different temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.

entry.title: Solving a non-abelian hidden subgroup problem on a trapped-ion quantum computer, examining how the measurement basis matters.
entry.summary: Solving a non-abelian hidden subgroup problem on a trapped-ion quantum computer: the power of the measurement basis arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper experimentally studies the hidden subgroup problem over q-hedral groups on the IonQ Forte trapped-ion quantum computer. It compares weak Fourier sampling, strong Fourier sampling in an adapted basis, adjacent-pair sampling, and forgetful abelian sampling. The hardware results largely match the theoretical predictions of Moore, Rockmore, Russell and Schulman. For p=7 and q=6, the device exceeds the success probability of an exhaustively optimised classical algorithm for up to three oracle queries.

entry.title: Phase-locked quantum battery charging through dissipative mode selection
entry.summary: Phase-Locked Quantum Battery Charging via Dissipative Mode Selection arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how dynamical instability and reservoir engineering can improve charging quality in a bosonic two-mode quantum battery. Dissipative coupling selectively amplifies a single unstable quasi-dark mode, giving phase-locked exponential charging at a lower gain threshold. Coherent coupling instead amplifies two frequency-split modes, producing persistent beating. The dissipative approach yields near-unit ergotropy fraction and a higher work-like signal-to-noise ratio.

entry.title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
entry.summary: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents QASPA-MaxCut, a shift-phase quantum circuit for the Max-Cut problem that encodes graph edges through controlled Ry rotations. The authors compare one-layer QASPA-MaxCut with depth-one QAOA using exact state-vector simulation on random backbone-augmented graphs and nineteen custom unweighted topologies. QAOA improves with more classical restarts, though the reported mean summaries remain lower than the QASPA selection scores.

entry.title: Experimental revival of hidden metrological steerability in noisy quantum channels via stochastic filtering
entry.summary: Experimental activation of hidden metrological steerability in quantum channels via stochastic filtering arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies steering-assisted quantum metrology, where a trusted party improves local phase estimation using classical information from an untrusted party. In phase-covariant amplitude-damping channels, stochastic pre- and post-filtering restores violation of the metrological steering inequality (MSI) that was initially absent. A photonic experiment with polarization qubits, a Sagnac interferometer, and Brewster-angle glass plates shows the critical damping parameter rising from about 0.5 to about 0.75. This comes at the cost of a reduced success probability.

entry.title: Calibrating flux crosstalk in tunable superconducting circuits, from zero prior knowledge to high precision
entry.summary: Flux Crosstalk Calibration from Zero Knowledge to High Precision in Fully Tunable Superconducting Circuits arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper addresses flux crosstalk in superconducting processors built from frequency-tunable qubits and couplers, which undermines independent flux control. It presents two methods that characterize coupler crosstalk without directly driving or measuring the couplers: zero-knowledge characterization, which uses intrinsic coupler-resonator coupling for fast estimates, and symmetric branch cancellation, which isolates crosstalk for high-precision quantification. Combined with an improved iterative procedure, residual coupler crosstalk is suppressed below 5×10⁻⁵.

entry.title: Precision limits and non-Gaussian advantages in optical phase estimation under preparation constraints
entry.summary: Precision Limits and Non-Gaussian Advantage in Optical Phase Estimation under Preparation Constraints arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies precision limits in optical quantum metrology for phase estimation. It introduces a constraint, an envelope on the photon-number distribution arising from physical limits of state-generation methods, that separates physically admissible probe states from inadmissible ones. Using this constraint for pure single-mode probes, the authors define a resource quantity N_RMS fixed by the preparation constraints and derive a finite bound on the quantum Fisher information whose Heisenberg scaling is attainable. They also identify a metrological advantage of non-Gaussian states over Gaussian probes under the same constraints.

entry.title: A counterexample to two conjectures about weak Gibbs and regularity properties
entry.summary: A Counterexample to the Weak Gibbs and Regularity Conjectures arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper constructs a counterexample that disproves the weak Gibbs conjecture and the regularity conjecture. The example is a spin-one system on the square lattice with a translation-invariant nearest-neighbor interaction. At high temperatures and high on-site field strengths, the system has a unique KMS state that lacks both the weak Gibbs and regularity properties.

entry.title: Cooling the environment to curb correlated atom loss in Rydberg arrays
entry.summary: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies how blackbody radiation triggers avalanche-like correlated atom loss in Rydberg atom arrays. Using a 45 K radiation shield, the authors reduce ambient blackbody radiation, which extends nS lifetimes and suppresses decay rates by 30% to 50%. Avalanche rates in cryogenic arrays drop in step with this suppression, and a parameter-free rate model matches the measurements.

entry.title: Parrondo's paradox in quantum walks with three distinct shift operators
entry.summary: Parrondo's paradox for three discrete-time quantum walks with distinct shift operators arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies Parrondo's paradox in discrete-time quantum walks, where combining biased walks can reverse the direction of the bias. The authors introduce a broad class of unitary shift operators that let a walker move left, right, or stay in place in each step. They show that the paradox can also occur with a single coin and three distinct shift operators. The work further examines how the paradox affects the time evolution of quantum entanglement between the walker and the coin.

entry.title: Spectral behavior of soft waveguides with twisted channels
entry.summary: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies a soft waveguide modeled by a Schrödinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel with a non-circular cross-section. It shows that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, a property expressed through a Hardy-type inequality. It also finds that a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum, and that a local slowdown of the twist can produce isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.

entry.title: A variational quantum algorithm for scheduling projects where workers have multiple skills.
entry.summary: A Variational Quantum Algorithm for Multi-Skill Project Scheduling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper applies a variational quantum algorithm to a multi-skill resource-constrained project scheduling problem, which accounts for worker capacities, skill matrices, task priorities, deadlines, and calendar stability during rescheduling. The authors solve the problem one day at a time with a logarithmic binary encoding that keeps each batch at or below 30 qubits. They compare entangling and entanglement-free circuits, training them with COBYLA and with Adam using SPSA gradients. For the instance studied, the entanglement-free reference also produced feasible schedules, and entanglement did not improve the solutions found.

entry.title: Quantum Advantage Needs Multiple Perspectives: A theory paper on the origins of quantum speedup
entry.summary: Quantum Advantage needs Multiple Perspectives arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a logical criterion for whether a quantum speedup is possible in continuous-variable and odd-prime qudit systems. It states that Wigner function nonnegativity signals the possibility of efficient classical simulation in the state-injection scenario. The authors argue that in any setting that cannot be efficiently simulated, the models for every measurement context cannot be merged into a single ZFC-satisfiable one, so quantum advantage requires multiple perspectives.

entry.title: Quasi-normal modes and thermalization in integrable quantum field theories via thermodynamic Bethe ansatz
entry.summary: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a thermodynamic Bethe ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. It interprets the exponential damping and oscillations seen when approaching thermal equilibrium as analogs of black hole quasi-normal mode frequencies from holography. The authors conjecture that this QNM TBA corresponds to an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded two-point correlators. They compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of the Ising CFT at nonzero temperature.

entry.title: Certifying Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories in 3D Translation-Invariant Stabilizer Codes
entry.summary: Universally Certifying Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories in 3D Translation-Invariant Stabilizer Codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents an algebraic-geometric framework for determining whether three-dimensional translation-invariant local stabilizer codes exhibit partial self-correction at finite temperature. It builds valuation matrices from algebraic curves defined by the codes' polynomials and derives a computable rank criterion. Combined with a polynomial-time decoder, codes meeting this criterion are shown to have super-Arrhenius memory lifetimes under local Davies dynamics.

entry.title: Beyond the Gap: Imaginary-Time Evolution and the Continuum Edge
entry.summary: Beyond the Gap: What Imaginary-Time Evolution Reveals About the Edge of the Continuum arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a mathematically rigorous method for extracting the spectral gap from imaginary-time evolution in infinite-dimensional Hamiltonians, where the first excitation often lies at the edge of a continuous spectrum. The authors show that detecting the gap depends on how the initial state and observable couple the ground state to excitations at the bottom of the continuum. When this coupling follows a power law, the gap and a logarithmic correction are recovered, and the correction's coefficient gives the spectral density exponent near the edge. Both predictions are confirmed numerically for an exactly solvable model.

entry.title: Helium State Calculation in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Using Photonic Quantum Circuits
entry.summary: Helium States in a CAS(2,2) Subspace Inspired by Quantum Photonics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper implements the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm on a four-mode Fock-state photonic system to compute ground and excited-state energies of the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) active space. The electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock representation and optimized with a continuous-variable circuit built from phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. In noiseless simulations, the ground and excited states retain unit survival probability within the target subspace, and results are benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the CASCI Hamiltonian.

entry.title: Constraining Lorentz violation using precision atomic spectroscopy
entry.summary: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines possible violations of Lorentz symmetry arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The authors model the effect with a modified dispersion relation, using a dimensionless coefficient suppressed by the Planck scale. Fitting high-precision spectroscopic data, they report a 95% confidence range for this coefficient. The paper notes that the heavy nucleus amplifies the signal at lowest order, while leptons dominate sensitivity at higher orders.

entry.title: Study of KPZ density hydrodynamics in a coherent XXZ-ASEP Lindbladian
entry.summary: Kardar--Parisi--Zhang density hydrodynamics in a coherent XXZ--ASEP Lindbladian arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies an XXZ chain with asymmetric Lindblad hopping whose stationary current has the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) form, although its populations do not evolve autonomously. The authors use the current curvature and static susceptibility to fix the leading Kardar–Parisi–Zhang length and amplitude. Analysis of the Liouvillian spectrum, real-space spreading, and Fourier relaxation supports KPZ scaling at the finite coherent couplings studied.

entry.title: Semi-Device-Independent Certification of Multi-Qubit Entangled Basis Measurements: a method for verifying a class of multi-qubit entangled basis measurements without fully trusting the devices.
entry.summary: Semi-Device-Independent Certification of multi-qubit Entangled Basis Measurement arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to certify multi-qubit entangled basis measurements, which matter for dense coding, quantum teleportation, and entanglement swapping, in a semi-device-independent way. It considers a prepare-and-measure scenario with two senders and one receiver, and builds nonlinear witnesses within a classical causal model framework. The optimal quantum value of the witness exceeds the classical bounds, which certifies the entangled basis measurement and the states prepared by the two senders.

entry.title: Linking Pulse and Circuit Levels: A Geometric Framework for Deterministic Error Suppression
entry.summary: Bridging Pulse and Circuit Levels: A Geometric Framework for Deterministic Error Suppression arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a circuit-level framework for dynamical quantum error correction that needs no logical encoding or ancillary qubits. The authors extend a geometric framework originally built for control-pulse-level error-correcting gates to the discrete dynamics of digital circuits, mapping coherent error accumulation to trajectories in a high-dimensional error space. Inserting deterministically optimized twirling gate sequences uses destructive interference to keep accumulated error bounded. The authors also show that this circuit-level correction works alongside pulse-level robust control, offering an analytical link between continuous noise dynamics and discrete quantum compilation.

entry.title: A scheme linking surface code patches via entanglement distillation without postselection
entry.summary: Connection of surface code patches based on entanglement distillation without postselection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a distributed surface-code quantum computing scheme that uses entanglement distillation without requiring postselection. Numerical simulations show the logical error rates are lower than in a setting without distillation. The authors further show that exploiting the asymmetry between spacelike and timelike errors in the surface code can suppress logical error rates more.

entry.title: Nanocavities that trap light in hBN to couple with single molecules' vibrations
entry.summary: Hyperbolic Nanocavities for Single-Molecule Vibrational Strong Coupling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper theoretically studies whether single-molecule vibrational strong coupling can be achieved in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) nanocavities. The nanocavities laterally confine hyperbolic phonon polaritons, and combined simulations reveal asymmetric resonances tunable by cavity aspect ratio. The authors report resonances with quality factors of about 600 and effective mode volumes near 10⁻⁷λ³, which they state suffice for transitions with dipole moments around 1 D.

entry.title: Cooling a superconducting qubit with a compact resistive dissipator tuned below its frequency
entry.summary: Resetting a Superconducting Qubit with a Compact Colder Resistive Dissipator below the Qubit Frequency arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a compact on-chip dissipator made of two transmon dissipation modes and a thin-film resistor, and experimentally demonstrates an unconditional reset protocol. Without extra control lines and with negligible impact on qubit T1, the transmon's effective temperature drops from 49 mK to 35 mK. Quantum process tomography gives a process error of 0.0028, and the protocol is robust to pulse parameter deviations.

entry.title: Spatial cost of recovering a fusion qubit in a critical spin chain.
entry.summary: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how much physical space is needed to recover a fusion qubit with vanishing error from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers–Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain. To leading order, the required span of physical spins is at least that of the shorter three-defect interval. An exact interval decoder is shown to attain this bound, and successful near-minimal supports concentrate on the shortest interval at leading order.

entry.title: Statistical mechanics of learnability in quantum codes, from generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
entry.summary: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies Bayesian inference of observables encoded in quantum codes under local weak measurements. The authors map the inference problem to classical spin models with generalized symmetries and use these symmetries to derive exact identities for the learnability of nonlocal observables. The results are demonstrated for the toric code, the X-cube model, and finite group quantum double models, including non-Abelian cases, which constrain which nonlocal information can be learned simultaneously.

entry.title: Robust geometric quantum gates for the QCCD trapped-ion architecture
entry.summary: Robust Geometric Gates for QCCD Architecture arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses how frequency offsets during ion shuttling in trapped-ion QCCD systems degrade gate fidelity. Using a room-temperature planar chip trap, the authors demonstrate a robust, universal single-qubit gate set based on a path-optimizable noncyclic geometric scheme. The gates keep dynamic noise suppressed even when shuttling operations are interleaved with gate execution, and the approach is validated in a system of up to 33 qubits.

entry.title: A new exact classical sampling method for Clifford+T quantum circuits that avoids computing marginal probabilities.
entry.summary: Classical Clifford+T Sampling without Computing Marginals arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces T-by-T sampling, an exact classical algorithm for sampling from Clifford+T circuits. For a circuit with T-count t, it needs only 2t amplitude evaluations on circuits with T-counts 1 through t, avoiding costly marginal probabilities. The number of evaluations does not depend on the surrounding Clifford structure, which suits low-rank stabiliser decompositions. The authors show it can sample magic state cultivation circuits up to distance 19 in a couple of seconds.

entry.title: Quantum computing study of entanglement asymmetry and the quantum Mpemba effect in field theory
entry.summary: Quantum Computing for Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Field Theory arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a quantum measurement protocol for estimating the Rényi entanglement asymmetry, which measures symmetry breaking at the subsystem level and can probe the quantum Mpemba effect. The protocol combines the SWAP test with a charge-resolving procedure based on randomized symmetry rotations. For a fixed additive accuracy ε, the required number of measurements scales as O(ε⁻²) without explicit dependence on total system size. The authors study the quantum Mpemba effect in the lattice Schwinger model with a θ term using classical state-vector simulations and estimate the resources needed to implement the protocol on NISQ devices, fault-tolerant quantum computers, and an early fault-tolerant architecture.

entry.title: A superradiant laser pumped collectively, with coherence scaling beyond the standard quantum limit.
entry.summary: Collectively pumped superradiant laser with coherence scaling beyond the standard quantum limit arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper notes that the standard quantum limit on laser coherence scales as μ², while the Heisenberg limit scales as μ⁴. The authors introduce generalized far-above-threshold laser models and show that an optical-frequency superradiant laser with feedback-controlled collective pumping realizes one of them. In the bad-cavity limit this laser's coherence can scale as μ^(8/3), surpassing the standard quantum limit.

entry.title: A method combining quantum sampling with DMRG to solve molecular energy problems
entry.summary: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization via Density Matrix Renormalization Group arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces SqDMRG, which combines sample-based quantum diagonalization with the density matrix renormalization group. It expands sampled determinant spaces into a product of fragment spaces and solves the Hamiltonian there using DMRG. The method is tested on benzene pentamer and decamer clusters with classical samples, and on the pentamer with quantum samples from an IBM quantum processor. It reaches sub-kcal/mol accuracy with far fewer configurations than direct diagonalization.

entry.title: How quantum systems can hold shared classical facts without being disturbed
entry.summary: The Structure of Shared Classical Facts in Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper asks whether perfectly matching local measurement outcomes necessarily form a shared classical record that does not disturb the system. For finite-dimensional multipartite states, it proves that nontrivial exact records are equivalent to a spectrum sharing structure with a unique finest decomposition into locally distinguishable sectors, where entanglement may persist. It also shows that even arbitrarily weak full-rank admixtures destroy exact sharing, while two-sided distance bounds quantify robustness through disturbance and disagreement.

entry.title: Rotated-frame determinant discovery for more efficient quantum configuration interaction in ground and excited states
entry.summary: Rotated-Frame Determinant Discovery for Ground- and Excited-State Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces rotate-sample-unrotate (RSU) determinant discovery to improve Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI). The method samples the same quantum state in complementary orbital frames and converts the observed determinants into a finite candidate set in the canonical basis, which is then diagonalized classically. The authors also combine RSU with the generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) for excited states. For N2 at a stretched geometry, RSU reaches chemical accuracy with 5,000 shots, compared with 20,000 shots for conventional QSCI.

entry.title: Hardware demo of neural-surrogate quantum MCMC for large constrained Boltzmann sampling
entry.summary: Hardware Demonstration of Neural-Surrogated Quantum-Enhanced MCMC for Large-Scale Constrained Boltzmann Sampling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper implements a hardware-efficient neural-surrogated quantum-enhanced MCMC method for Boltzmann sampling on an IBM Quantum Heron r2 processor. Experiments with 144 binary variables show faster autocorrelation decay for suitable subproblem sizes, while neural-surrogate learning becomes harder for larger blocks. For a 1064-variable system, the autocorrelation decay rate per MCMC step is about 5.2 and 12.3 times that of global and local Kawasaki dynamics, respectively.

entry.title: Quantum advantage in imaging by suppressing coherent noise
entry.summary: Quantum Advantage in Sensing and Imaging through Coherent Nuisance Suppression arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces a relational Fourier sampling algorithm for optimal, source-independent imaging with a programmable quantum camera. A quantum receiver processes samples jointly to access observables in which common nuisance parameters, such as aberrations and drift, are suppressed. The authors argue this yields an exponential reduction in sample complexity and predict over three orders of magnitude fewer photons for resolving point sources under typical ground-based seeing conditions.

entry.title: Efficiently Tracking Errors and Outcomes in Universal Quantum Circuits
entry.summary: Efficiently tracking errors and outcomes in universal quantum circuits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a method for efficiently simulating error propagation and decoding in universal fault-tolerant quantum circuits under stochastic Pauli noise. It uses a modified Pauli frame that carries no logical information, and decoding success is checked by verifying the frame is logically trivial afterward. The approach can also simulate adaptive operations conditioned on logical measurements when their outcome distributions are known. The method only detects decoding failures and cannot sample the noiseless outcome distribution of the logical circuit.

entry.title: Symmetry-guided variational quantum optimization algorithms
entry.summary: Symmetry-guided algorithms for variational quantum optimization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes symmetry-guided variational quantum algorithms that use a quantum-accessible Hilbert-Schmidt asymmetry measure, which quantifies how far a state deviates from invariance under a symmetry group. The measure steers optimization toward a target symmetry sector without enforcing the symmetry on the preparation circuit. The approach is tested on variational eigensolver calculations for singlet ground states with collective SU(2) symmetry, including a five-qubit two-cluster Hamiltonian and collective spin models with up to 12 particles. Compared with direct energy minimization, the authors report improved energy accuracy during optimization and higher ground-state fidelity.

entry.title: Classical records and Bell correlations in a dynamically formed quantum body
entry.summary: Classical records and Bell correlations in a dynamically formed quantum body arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how competing quantum contacts can create a boundary in a subsystem that originally had none. The authors build approximately isolated bodies from bare field vacuum and zero-centred contact packets. On the formed material spins, coarse collective records appear before an all-outcome Bell violation. The analysis keeps the finite bath, residual boundary interaction, failed records and preparation costs, with results stated for polynomial resources.

entry.title: Exact two-body density-matrix spectrum of a one-dimensional fermion gas
entry.summary: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper derives the complete spectrum of the two-body density matrix for the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas, starting from its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. It gives analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for any particle number and distinguishes collective states from single-determinant states. The authors also provide an asymptotic expansion of the largest eigenvalue, which scales linearly with particle number, and discuss the link between collective states and composite bosons.

entry.title: Polariton condensates that resist compression, enabling larger spin-system simulations
entry.summary: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies driven-dissipative polariton networks as an analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. The authors propose an in situ mechanism in which higher-order nonlinear loss drives condensates into an incompressible regime, suppressing amplitude fluctuations and enforcing phase-only dynamics. For XY networks of up to 10,000 spins, they report a more than 50-fold energy reduction, and weak Hermitian pulses help the system escape local minima.

entry.title: Coherence spreading law in quenched uniform Bose gases
entry.summary: Coherence Spreading Law in Quenched Homogeneous Bose Gases arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how coherence spreads in uniform bosonic gases after a sudden quench, using both analytical and numerical methods. It shows that the squared coherence length grows linearly in time, with the spreading law depending on the ratio of initial energy to healing energy. When this ratio is small, the growth rate depends only on Planck's constant divided by particle mass, not on interaction strength or initial momentum distribution. The paper also identifies the conditions under which this universality holds.

entry.title: Exact teleportation limits for fermionic Hawking thermality beyond single-mode approximation
entry.summary: Exact teleportation bounds for fermionic Hawking thermality beyond the single-mode approximation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies fermionic teleportation near a Schwarzschild horizon by separating Hawking thermal mixing from the composition of right and left Unruh modes. For fixed mode composition, it solves a global constrained quantum-channel optimization over all two-qubit resource states whose fully entangled fraction stays at or below the standard teleportation threshold before thermal mixing. The solution gives an exact necessary-and-sufficient activation boundary, a second boundary for reaching the universal optimum, and explicit optimizing states.

entry.title: Static and dynamical Casimir effects in a wedge: a worldline study
entry.summary: Static and dynamical Casimir effects in a wedge within the worldline formulation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies a massless scalar field confined to a wedge with a semitransparent arc that can oscillate radially, using the worldline formulation. The effective action is expanded in the arc's radial displacement, yielding in closed form the wedge's Casimir energy and the arc's contribution at zeroth order. The second-order term determines the probability of particle pair creation by the moving arc, and its behavior in the narrow-wedge limit is analyzed. The authors also decompose the electromagnetic field into TE and TM scalars to obtain Casimir energies for wedges with perfectly conducting, perfectly permeable, and mixed walls.

entry.title: Most entangled states of four and seven qubits
entry.summary: The most entangled states of four and seven qubits arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how entangled pure states of four and seven qubits can be on average across balanced splits. For four qubits, it proves the Higuchi–Sudbery conjecture, bounding the mean von Neumann entropy of the three 2|2 cuts. For seven qubits, it finds bounds on the mean purity and mean entropy over the 35 balanced 3|4 cuts, each with a unique optimal state. The paper also proves the Gour–Wallach conjecture for Rényi entropies of all orders.

entry.title: Exact mirror-parity selection rule for electron-phonon coupling in two-dimensional crystals
entry.summary: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper derives a symmetry selection rule for electron-phonon scattering in two-dimensional crystals with a horizontal mirror plane.
