entry.summary: Runtime Compilation for Quantum Circuits with PQF-Enabled R_z Synthesis arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper addresses reducing T-gate counts in fault-tolerant quantum computing with surface codes. It proposes R²-PQF, a runtime routing protocol that dynamically computes lattice-surgery paths for circuits synthesized with PQF, implemented via a wavefront breadth-first search on FPGA and ASIC. For a 300-qubit Ising Hamiltonian circuit, the median logical time-step is 1.51 µs, and the method is reported to be 1.34× faster on average than a stalling baseline, and up to 1.76× faster.

entry.title: Gaussian quantum integrated sensing and communication: a quantum scheme that communicates over an optical link while locating a defect, and studies how to split shared entanglement between the two tasks
entry.summary: Gaussian Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies a quantum integrated sensing and communication problem over an optical link, where a low-power transmitter communicates with a receiver while locating a defect that produces a backscattered signal. The system is modeled as a lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel, and two protocols are proposed that use shared Gaussian entanglement, either two-mode or three-mode squeezed vacuum states, to assist both sensing and communication. The results characterize achievable communication-rate and sensing error-exponent regions, which outperform time-sharing schemes and demonstrate a quantum advantage.

entry.title: Weyl superfluids from trivial bands via interaction in an optical Raman lattice
entry.summary: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a way to realize Weyl superfluidity in the strongly correlated regime of a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice, using pairing that arises from the interplay of large Zeeman splitting and strong Hubbard interaction. Mean-field calculations yield Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, as well as fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning interaction strength and filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. An experimental implementation with ultracold potassium-40 atoms is also proposed.

entry.title: Sharp entropy uncertainty bounds for discrete quantum quasiprobability distributions
entry.summary: Tight Quasiprobabilistic Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Discrete Quantum Systems arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies entropic uncertainty for quasiprobability distributions in discrete quantum systems. The authors prove that for Kirkwood-Dirac distributions built from mutually unbiased bases and for Gross-Wigner distributions, the entropy lower bound is attained by pure states with positive quasiprobability distributions. They also show that Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with large nonpositivity have large uncertainty.

entry.title: Adaptive qubit encoding for optimizing continuous variables on quantum hardware.
entry.summary: Adaptive Qubit Encoding for Continuous-Variable Quantum Optimization arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a framework for optimizing continuous-variable functions on qubit-based quantum hardware. It combines adaptive discretization with an iterative local mapping of the objective onto an effective spin-glass Hamiltonian. The method is tested on unconstrained and constrained n-dimensional Gramacy-Lee benchmarks and on a proof-of-concept inverse-planning problem in intensity-modulated radiotherapy for cancer treatment. The results indicate the framework can produce competitive solutions.

entry.title: How internal electric fields affect precise diamond magnetometry
entry.summary: The Impact of Internal Electric Fields on Accurate Diamond Magnetometry arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how random internal electric fields, caused by charged dopants in diamond, shift the spin-transition frequencies of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers and affect magnetometry accuracy. The authors built a Monte Carlo model that reproduces the asymmetric spectral lineshapes seen in experiments and used it to quantify the resulting errors. Standard analysis shows systematic errors above the g-factor uncertainty below about 5 mT, and the proposed fitting function reduces this error by nearly an order of magnitude.

entry.title: A method for describing unitary matrices, applied to nucleon-nucleon scattering matrices above the inelastic threshold.
entry.summary: Parametrization of unitary matrices, parametrizing the symmetric S matrix and the NN S matrix above the inelastic threshold arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper notes that existing S-matrix representations used to analyze nucleon-nucleon (NN) scattering above the inelastic threshold do not simultaneously satisfy implicit unitarity, generality, and a connection to low-energy (Stapp) parameters. The author presents an S-matrix representation that meets these requirements and can be used to solve the corresponding inverse scattering problem. As a by-product, a parametrization of an n-dimensional unitary matrix is derived.

entry.title: How quantizing the pump changes optimal measurements in quantum sensing
entry.summary: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines quantum phase sensing when the pump light is treated as a quantum object rather than an undepleted classical resource, as earlier analyses assumed. It finds that quantum advantage persists after pump quantization but depends critically on the nonlinear (χ⁽²⁾) source dynamics. Heisenberg scaling is reached in the regime of strong pump depletion, where signal flux is maximized, and this requires a joint nonlinear measurement of the whole pump-signal system rather than standard photon counting.

entry.title: Effective non-Hermitian dynamics from post-selection methods
entry.summary: Non-Hermitian effective dynamics from post-selection protocols arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper shows that Feshbach projection, the Lindblad master equation, and the ancilla approach can all be unified through the Kraus map formalism, yielding non-Hermitian time evolution once an appropriate post-selection procedure is applied. It derives an exact expression for conditional system dynamics and examines the approximations of each approach and the non-Hermitian Hamiltonians they produce. The authors justify the right-right formalism for computing expectation values and conclude that traditional thermodynamic equilibrium does not apply to general non-Hermitian systems.

entry.title: Paper on unital qubit channels being 3-noisy, i.e., simulable with a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment
entry.summary: Unital qubit channels are 3-noisy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies algebraic and environmental properties of mixed unitary quantum operations. It shows that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is again n-noisy, and that this property is invariant under unitary equivalence. Using majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, the authors demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated with a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment.

entry.title: Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillian operators
entry.summary: Liouvillian Kramers Degeneracy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper shows that time-reversal and parity symmetries together enforce Kramers degeneracy in Liouvillian superoperators acting on mixed states. The authors construct dissipative many-body models of interacting fermions and spins that exhibit this degeneracy. Their complex spectral statistics follow the non-Hermitian random matrix ensembles of the corresponding symplectic class.

entry.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning with physics-informed neural networks
entry.summary: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) method for learning control fields that implement one- and two-qubit quantum gates, trained with the time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Unitary simulations report very low average gate infidelities for Hadamard and controlled-NOT gates under several interaction types. The authors also test the control fields under dephasing and amplitude damping, and show that boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions can compactly represent the learned controls.

entry.title: Quantum circuit optimization that splits circuits optimally and accounts for entanglement
entry.summary: Entanglement-Aware Quantum Circuit Optimization through Globally Optimal Partitioning arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper presents a scalable framework that selects globally optimal partitions of a quantum circuit using an integer linear program, with objectives such as minimizing partition count or weighted execution cost. The selected partitions are resynthesized with an operator-Schmidt rank (OSR) based method that exploits their internal entanglement. On 772 local unitary targets, OSR produced 741 verified syntheses versus 617 for BQSKit, and matched or reduced CNOT counts in all 617 jointly verified pairs.

entry.title: Rebuilding the conformal algebra from a critical ground state on the (fuzzy) sphere
entry.summary: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper builds on earlier work that reconstructs the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory ground state. It develops methods to construct the full global conformal algebra and tests them using fuzzy sphere regularization. These methods outperform constructions based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, need no extra tuning, and improve with system size. The authors also identify conformal primary states and provide further support for a model of short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian.

entry.title: Optimized finite-key security for satellite uplink entangled quantum key distribution
entry.summary: Optimised finite key for satellite up-link entangled quantum key distribution arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies entanglement-based quantum key distribution from ground to satellite, using a more rigorous security analysis that accounts for finite-size effects from short block lengths. It finds that the optimal source operation changes slightly under finite statistics, with the pump power should be slightly lowered. The authors estimate annual key rates for the Heriot-Watt ground station and several satellite parameters, finding that accumulating all raw key material before extracting a secure key yields a higher annual key rate.

entry.title: A quantum banking system that uses quantum tokens to secure cash withdrawals
entry.summary: Quantum banking system for secure cash withdrawal arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper proposes a quantum-secure cash withdrawal framework that replaces reproducible classical credentials with quantum tokens for authentication. It integrates token generation, authentication, and verification into existing banking workflows using experimentally motivated quantum control techniques. According to the authors, the approach is intended to mitigate card cloning, credential theft, and counterfeiting.

entry.title: Renormalised hydrogen partition function and Saha ionisation equation
entry.summary: Renormalisation of Hydrogen Partition Function and Saha Ionisation Equation arXiv · Oct 16, 2026The paper addresses the divergence of the neutral hydrogen atom partition function that appears in the Saha ionisation equation, caused by the rapidly growing degeneracy of excited states. The authors propose a regularisation and renormalisation procedure that yields a well-defined partition function. This allows calculation of energy level populations and ionisation state of hydrogen plasma versus temperature and pressure. The results reduce to the Saha equation at low temperatures and describe deviations from it at higher temperatures, with application to the solar core and atmosphere considered.

entry.title: Entanglement Resource Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
entry.summary: Entanglement Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how a limited pool of entanglement can support both communication and distributed sensing in future quantum networks. It proposes a network-level quantum integrated sensing and communication (Q-ISAC) framework in which a quantum base station dynamically allocates Bell pairs and partitions sensing resources among multiple GHZ probes. The authors model effective quantum Fisher information and solve the allocation problem with a hierarchical constrained proximal policy optimization (HC-PPO) method. Numerical results show that GHZ probing needs about 27 to 30 percent fewer sensing qubits than separable probing under the same sensing requirements.

entry.title: Hardware-aware design of quantum reservoir computing for insurance claims forecasting
entry.summary: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether small quantum reservoir computing models can forecast next-day motor-insurance claim counts competitively with classical models, and whether their predictions hold up on noisy hardware. A six-qubit gate-based reservoir was evaluated on 232 held-out test days, where four of five candidates did not differ significantly from ridge regression. On the IBM Kingston processor, hardware-aware qubit layouts gave lower error than Qiskit's default layouts in every paired round.

entry.title: Factorized Approximate Inverse Preconditioners for Tensor Train Solvers
entry.summary: Factorized approximate inverse preconditioners in the tensor train format arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents a preconditioning method that speeds up Tensor Train (TT) solvers for symmetric positive-definite linear systems. The authors extend the Factorized Sparse Approximate Inverse framework to tensor networks, building the preconditioner as the product of a TT operator and its transpose, which satisfies the requirements of the Conjugate Gradient method. Tests on anisotropic diffusion and Poisson problems show consistent reductions in iterations, with net speedups of up to 25% in ill-conditioned time-stepping settings. The authors also introduce the open-source Julia library DifferenTT.jl.

entry.title: Certifying particle indistinguishability in interferometers without tailored hardware
entry.summary: Marginal bunching for in situ certification of multiparticle indistinguishability arXiv · Oct 19, 2026The paper proposes a scalable, efficient in situ method to test whether identical bosons or fermions are indistinguishable in linear interferometer experiments. It applies to any generic linear interferometer. For particles in distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the required number of runs scales polynomially with particle number, interferometer size, and inverse precision, with high probability. The method remains polynomial under uniform particle loss if the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose an in situ method to certify multiparticle indistinguishability in linear interferometers, exploiting quantum parallelism and bunching/anti-bunching tendencies. They report that fo

entry.title: Maximum purity of absolutely separable and PPT quantum states in qutrit-qudit systems
entry.summary: Maximum purity of absolutely separable and absolutely PPT states in qutrit--qudit systems arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies bipartite quantum states in qutrit-qudit systems C^3⊗C^n with n≥3. It determines the maximum purity of absolutely separable states and absolutely PPT states, showing both classes share the same maximum. The authors also bound the minimum partial-transpose eigenvalue reachable by global unitary transformations in terms of purity and characterize the states attaining this bound. These results confirm the inscribed-polytope purity conjecture for all qutrit-qudit systems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that absolutely separable and absolutely PPT qutrit-qudit states in C³⊗Cⁿ (n≥3) share the same maximum purity, confirming the inscribed-polytope conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda and

entry.title: Quantum hypothesis testing that can refuse to decide: exact error-exponent trade-off
entry.summary: Binary Quantum Hypothesis Testing with a Rejection Option: The Exact Error-Exponent Trade-off arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies binary quantum hypothesis testing on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, where the test may reject, and the rejection probabilities under both hypotheses must vanish exponentially. It gives necessary and sufficient conditions for a quadruple of error and rejection exponents to be achievable, consisting of three single-letter conditions. Two involve Petz–Rényi quantities and match a converse bound conjectured to be tight by Ji and Regula, while the third involves α–z Rényi quantities. The proof combines a sector decomposition within Schur–Weyl blocks, an explicit one-shot measurement construction, and an exact minimax argument. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give an exact characterization of the error-exponent trade-off for binary quantum hypothesis testing with rejection, report that two conditions match the Ji-Regula conjectured tight bound,

entry.title: Quantum lower bounds for finding and testing k-to-one collisions in strings
entry.summary: Quantum Lower Bounds for Collision Problems arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper studies quantum query complexity for Promised k-to-one Finding on an exactly k-to-one string over a fixed alphabet. It gives tight lower bounds for both adaptive algorithms and one-round non-adaptive algorithms, the latter matching classical birthday sampling even with entangled queries. It also proves a non-adaptive lower bound for k-to-one Testing, resolving an open question from Koiran, Landes, Portier, and Yao. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report tight adaptive and one-round non-adaptive quantum query lower bounds for promised k-to-one finding on exactly k-to-one inputs, with the one-round bound matching classical birthday s

entry.title: Full-order mutual information from modular flow, without replicas
entry.summary: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper derives an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic d-dimensional CFTs. It uses a radial sewing expansion, a modular response formula for relative entropy, and geometric modular flow, avoiding replica-number analytic continuation. In the two-dimensional Ising CFT, the first ten radial orders are computed and show good agreement with lattice data at finite separation.

entry.title: Lee-Yang theorems for q-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK
entry.summary: Lee-Yang theorems for q-deformed oscillators and doubly-scaled SYK arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proves that the vacuum partition function of the q-deformed oscillator has all its zeros on the imaginary axis (the Lee-Yang property) for every q in [-1,1), confirming conjectures by Okuyama from 2023. Using the link between q-deformed oscillators and the doubly-scaled SYK Hamiltonian, the authors show that the annealed SYK partition function has the same property in the thermodynamic limit. They conclude that the quenched SYK partition function has a zero-free strip of constant width with high probability. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the q-deformed oscillator partition function has Lee-Yang zeros and extend this to doubly-scaled SYK.

entry.title: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy: a theoretical study on reducing electron beam energy spread via strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures
entry.summary: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper addresses the brightness limits of electron sources in electron microscopes by proposing single-pass stochastic cooling inside the microscope, using strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures. The approach is laser-free, compatible with continuous-wave operation, and aims to improve longitudinal emittance without loss. The authors develop a fully quantum mechanical model valid in the strong coupling regime and derive an analytic asymptotic formula for the optimal cooled energy spread. Numerical simulations show that reduced energy spread corresponds to higher electron quantum state purity and smaller longitudinal phase space area.

entry.title: Unifying entanglement and nonclassicality through the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum
entry.summary: Unifying entanglement and nonclassicality via the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies the relationship between quantum entanglement and nonclassicality, which is known to be linked through two-mode mixing. The authors extend this connection to arbitrary multimode Gaussian evolutions. They use the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum to quantify single-mode phase-space nonclassicality and derive sufficient conditions for a single-mode state to generate NPT entanglement after a multimode Gaussian unitary evolution. These conditions tighten and generalize existing criteria.

entry.title: Quantum tomography in Schwartz space, a function-space framework for reconstructing quantum states
entry.summary: Quantum tomography on Schwartz space arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper shows that standard quantum tomography results, usually proven in Hilbert spaces, can also be established within the theory of Schwartz spaces. It shows that quantum states are equivalently characterized by their Wigner function, the characteristic function of that Wigner function, and the probability distributions of linear combinations of position and momentum. The techniques are presented in a form more accessible to physicists.

entry.title: Exceptional points and optimized encoding in qubit stabilizer codes
entry.summary: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies stabilizer codes under continuous blind stabilizer measurements, casting error correction as a Liouvillian spectral problem where Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. The authors show this competition generically produces Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is limited by the code distance, and that these points accelerate the decay of encoded coherences. They then optimize the logical qubit encoding using Lindblad operator eigenmodes and apply it to the [[5,1,3]] code, where it outperforms naive encoding near the exceptional point.

entry.title: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence
entry.summary: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper theoretically studies how trapped electric charges on dielectric mirrors affect the specular reflection and diffuse scattering of hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium atoms at grazing incidence on SiO2/Si and MgF2 surfaces. The authors show that the charge distribution determines the polarization potential seen by the atoms, which changes the threshold behavior of reflection. At a surface charge density of 10^12 cm^-2, absorption increases by up to 26% for SiO2/Si and by two to three times for MgF2.

entry.title: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
entry.summary: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proves propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. The authors construct local representatives of evolved interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth. The threshold a > d_vol is shown to be optimal in general. The results yield dynamical estimates for perturbation theory with extensive perturbations. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give lossless propagation bounds for fermionic interactions with polynomial growth and prove the threshold a>d_vol is optimal, with applications to gap stability and adiabatic theory.

entry.title: Faster thermalization of 1D noncommuting Hamiltonians using system-bath interactions with linearly many ancillas
entry.summary: Efficient thermalization of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians via system-bath interactions with Theta(n) ancilla qubits arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proves rapid convergence of a system-bath algorithm that prepares Gibbs states of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians at any fixed positive temperature. For a chain of n qudits, it reaches trace-norm error ε in expected total evolution time Õ(n/ε). This improves the previously proved Õ(n^6/ε) bound for single-ancilla samplers, up to logarithmic factors. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the bound for single-ancilla system-bath Gibbs samplers from O(n^6) to linear system-size dependence, with theoretical analysis.

entry.title: Quartet state of the neutral nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond and optimized near-infrared spin readout
entry.summary: Quartet state of the neutral nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond and optimized spin readout under near-infrared two-photon excitation arXiv · Nov 3, 2026After photoionization, the nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond leaves a neutral defect in a metastable quartet state of unknown energy. Using tunable femtosecond two-photon optically detected magnetic resonance, the authors find the spin-contrast onset at 1.23 ± 0.02 eV and place the quartet 0.54 ± 0.04 eV above the neutral ground state. This threshold makes 1060–1075 nm the optimal excitation for spin readout, giving 26–37% higher shot-noise-limited sensitivity than 1030–1040 nm.

entry.title: Agentic Pipeline Verifying Topological Code Mapping to Quantum Hardware via Lean
entry.summary: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents an AI-agent-assisted workflow that uses the Lean proof assistant to check whether an effective device Hamiltonian preserves the intended low-energy subspace of a target many-body Hamiltonian. It applies the method to topological quantum error correction, building the ideal Hamiltonian from qubits and parity checks and comparing three bounds on unwanted energy shifts. In an eight-qubit toric-code array on a superconducting device, an AI agent finds device parameters within a leakage budget, and Lean verifies four isolated low-energy states close to the ideal code space.

entry.title: Learning stabilizer structure under global depolarizing noise with polynomial copies
entry.summary: Stabilizer Learning under Global Depolarizing Noise with Polynomial Copies and 2^t Time arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how to learn the stabilizer structure of an unknown pure n-qubit state observed through global depolarizing noise of unknown strength, using destructive two-copy Bell measurements. It gives a learner that uses polynomially many copies and 2^t times polynomial classical time, for any fixed noise bound below one. This answers an open question from Tang and Steckmann by exceeding their earlier noise threshold of about 0.16. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend the noise threshold from about 0.16 to any fixed global depolarizing bound below one, with polynomial copies and 2^t time.

entry.title: Controlling phase between cores of multi-core fiber inline using a commercial polarization controller
entry.summary: Inline inter-core phase control in multi-core fiber with a commercial polarization controller arXiv · Nov 3, 2026Phase control between cores is needed for interferometry in multi-core fiber, but no compact inline device exists for this. The authors show that a commercial, low-loss inline polarization controller can work as an inline inter-core phase shifter. In two-core interferometry on a four-core patchcord, one device gave a reversible phase of 0.95 ± 0.02 rad, with a lower bound of 0.38 rad independent of operating point.

entry.title: Dynamics of Fock states in traveling pulses
entry.summary: Dynamics of Fock states in traveling pulses arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how the quantum state of a traveling light pulse changes the excitation dynamics of a two-level atom, comparing coherent and Fock input states. Coherent pulses produce damped Rabi oscillations, while Fock pulses show partial recovery of oscillation amplitude in the trailing part of the pulse. The authors examine the roles of an auxiliary temporal mode and radiative loss, and connect the effect to stimulated Raman adiabatic passage.

entry.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates for quantum advantage
entry.summary: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies a chain of dense SYK dots linked by single ZZ bonds, a model whose ground states are highly entangled. It gives an upper bound on entanglement across any cut and estimates the dot size at which a quantum advantage could appear. The estimate suggests dots of roughly 15 to 21 qubits or more, with two-qubit error rates near 10^-6 needed per Trotter step. Numerical tests with imaginary-time matrix product states and variational circuits support these assumptions.

entry.title: Universal growth and classical-like dynamics of Krylov complexity
entry.summary: Universality and Emergent Classicality in Krylov Space arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how Krylov complexity grows linearly at late times in many systems. It gives a general spectral formula for the leading growth coefficients of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, without needing detailed Lanczos coefficients. For states with narrow energy distributions, dynamics in the Krylov basis resembles motion along a classical trajectory. The results are demonstrated for the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK, where chord-number moments are computed through one-loop order.

entry.title: Controlling a macroscopic free mass via continuous quantum measurement
entry.summary: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper realizes a suspended 1-milligram rotor operating in the free-particle regime with strong environmental isolation. The researchers directly resolve thermal fluctuations in its motion, with a damping rate of only 7 nHz. Through continuous quantum measurement, they localize the otherwise unconfined motion, obtaining conditional states with entropic temperatures as low as 140 nK. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report controlling a 1-milligram suspended rotor in the free-particle regime via continuous quantum measurement, reaching 140 nK and applying it to tests of quantum gravity.

entry.title: Correlated catalysis eliminates the strong converse in entanglement distillation
entry.summary: Correlated Catalysis Removes the Strong Converse for Entanglement Distillation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies entanglement distillation, which converts noisy shared quantum states into maximally entangled pairs using local operations and classical communication. It shows that correlated catalysis removes the strong converse for every distillable bipartite state. At any target rate above the distillable entanglement E_D, the optimal asymptotic fidelity equals E_D/R. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that correlated catalysis removes the strong converse, giving optimal fidelity E_D/R above the distillation rate.

entry.title: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes: A study of a new quantum gas microscope that measures position and momentum together, to probe correlations in strongly interacting quantum matter.
entry.summary: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper examines the recently proposed phase-space microscope, which measures position and momentum jointly in a single shot. The authors show that n-body correlation functions built from these snapshots can in principle determine all n-body observables of a many-body quantum state. Applications include witnessing entanglement hidden from both position and momentum, resolving pairing structure across the BEC-BCS crossover, and measuring the local Chern marker.

entry.title: Physical origin of the Berry connection for free relativistic electrons
entry.summary: On physical origin of Berry connection of free relativistic electrons arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper addresses the unresolved question of which operators correctly describe the spin and orbital angular momentum of free relativistic electrons, and challenges the belief that a spin-orbit coupling arises through the Berry connection. The authors argue that only observables projected onto the positive-energy subspace of the Dirac equation represent physical electron quantities. They conclude that the Berry connection describes the position of a quantum reference point relative to the laboratory frame.

entry.title: Second-order mean force Gibbs state of fermionic open systems: a paper deriving the equilibrium state of fermionic systems coupled to a reservoir, checked against exact numerics.
entry.summary: Second-order mean force Gibbs state of fermionic open systems arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper derives the grand canonical mean force Gibbs (MFG) state for a generic fermionic system coupled to a thermal reservoir at arbitrary chemical potential, to second order in the coupling. It uses the mode reduced state to make the fermionic MFG state well defined and splits the correction to the bare Gibbs state into particle and hole channels. The results are applied to the resonant level model, two modes sharing a reservoir, and the single impurity Anderson model, and checked against numerically exact and real-time dynamical calculations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive a second-order grand canonical mean force Gibbs state for fermionic systems and compare it with numerically exact and real-time results.

entry.title: Nonreciprocal Bell-state generation via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system
entry.summary: Nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper proposes a scheme for generating Bell states nonreciprocally in a system of a superconducting qubit and a magnon-hosting yttrium iron garnet sphere. Both are coupled to a shared waveguide, producing cooperative dissipation that creates a dark eigenstate in the single-excitation subspace. Reversing the bias magnetic field makes this dark state correspond to a different Bell state. A fidelity-based nonreciprocal rate is defined to quantify the effect.

entry.title: Generating needle-shaped beams from SPDC photons with flat, inverse-designed optics
entry.summary: Needle-beam generation from SPDC photons using inverse-designed flat optics arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The study uses a compact inverse-designed multilevel diffractive lens to produce needle-like beams from spontaneous parametric downconversion light. A heralded three-detector measurement before the lens confirms the nonclassical nature of the source, with a zero-delay second-order correlation of about 0.14. Under collinear illumination, the lens keeps the focus tightly confined over about 11 mm, showing less diffraction broadening than a conventional plano-convex lens.

entry.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
entry.summary: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces eigenkit, a quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. It supports 12 execution providers, including simulators and quantum hardware, and integrates with NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn. Experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that the better processor for a given algorithm depends on how well the algorithm's topology matches the processor's physical connectivity.

entry.title: Using pulse sequences to boost group light emission from mixed quantum emitters
entry.summary: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how a periodic pulse sequence can strengthen cooperative behavior in a group of quantum emitters that have different spectral frequencies. The authors combine a semi-analytical mean-field solution with a digital quantum simulation to examine coherence and emitted intensity versus spectral disparity, time, atom number, and inter-pulse delay. They report clear signs of enhanced cooperative dynamics when enough pulses suppress dephasing during an emitter's lifetime. This suggests externally applied control fields as a tuning method for ensemble dynamics after fabrication.

entry.title: Routing Strategies for High-Rate Error Correction on Spin Qubits
entry.summary: Towards Optimal Routing Strategies for qLDPC codes on Silicon Spin Qubits arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how to implement qLDPC quantum error correction codes on silicon spin qubits by shuttling qubits next to each other when they need to interact. It analyzes memory experiments of the [[144,12,12]] Gross code on square and diagonal-augmented grids, comparing three shuttling strategies, initial layouts, and shuttling noise models. The best strategy minimizes the longest distance travelled rather than the total distance.

entry.title: Probing multiphoton transitions between dressed states in a strongly driven Jaynes–Cummings system with quantum-nondemolition readout
entry.summary: Quantum-Nondemolition Probing of Multiphoton Transitions between Dressed States in a Strongly Driven Jaynes--Cummings System arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies the spectroscopy of the Jaynes–Cummings model, which describes a qubit coupled to a cavity, under strong driving in circuit quantum electrodynamics. The authors separate the strong cavity drive from qubit readout, which substantially improves measurement sensitivity compared with conventional cavity-transmission spectroscopy. They identify near-resonant features as multiphoton transitions between dressed states of the same parity and resolve transitions between dressed states of opposite parity. Away from resonance, selective enhancement and suppression of multiphoton transitions are also observed.

entry.title: unitaryQIP = unitaryPSPACE: equality of two unitary synthesis complexity classes
entry.summary: unitaryQIP = unitaryPSPACE arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies the computational cost of applying a target unitary to an unknown quantum state. It proves that the unitary complexity classes unitaryQIP and unitaryPSPACE are equal, an analogue of the earlier QIP=PSPACE and stateQIP=statePSPACE results. The authors also show the protocol can be parallelized to constant rounds when the verifier receives polynomially many input copies, and identify a complexity-theoretic barrier to proving the existence of EFI pairs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors extend QIP=PSPACE to unitary synthesis, proving unitaryQIP=unitaryPSPACE via an acceptance rigidity lemma and a PSPACE-oracle synthesis construction.

entry.title: Coulomb blockade in a one-dimensional array of strong Josephson junctions
entry.summary: Coulomb Blockade in a One-Dimensional Array of Strong Josephson Junctions arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The study measures current in a voltage-biased long array of Josephson junctions. The current-voltage curves show no critical current but instead a threshold voltage and finite activation energy, consistent with Coulomb blockade. The energy scale is much smaller than a single island's geometric capacitance predicts, which the authors attribute to strong quantum charge fluctuations from a large Josephson energy.

entry.title: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases
entry.summary: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases arXiv · Nov 2, 2026Chiral Floquet phases carry quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized. This paper identifies a related effect, called Hilbert-space pumping, in which a quantized-dimension part of the boundary Hilbert space moves between opposite boundaries under a time-translation-twisted boundary condition. For noninteracting fermions the number of transferred modes is set by the winding number, and for interacting systems with quantum cellular automaton boundary dynamics it is set by the GNVW index.

entry.title: Single-port homodyne detection achieves optimal multiphase sensing in a ring cavity
entry.summary: Single-port homodyne detection achieves optimal multiphase sensing in an n-port ring cavity arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies estimating the n internal phases of a lossless n-port ring cavity simultaneously, probed by a fixed-energy multimode coherent state. It gives a necessary and sufficient condition for the global optimum: equal energy distribution among the ports and a phase-matching condition for each port. At this optimum the quantum Fisher information matrix is full rank, and balanced homodyne detection at each output port attains the optimal Fisher information.

entry.title: Inferring entanglement from quantum-eraser measurement records
entry.summary: Entanglement inference from quantum erasure and path discrimination arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper determines the minimum entanglement compatible with quantum-eraser data when the preparation may be mixed. For noisy GHZ states it gives sharp entanglement-depth thresholds with matching converses, and it shows how parity information strengthens certification. For an ideal three-qubit eraser, it classifies the additional marker measurement directions that certify genuine multipartite entanglement.

entry.title: Quantum teleportation with photon-added versus photon-subtracted two-mode squeezed Fock states
entry.summary: Quantum teleportation using photon-added two-mode squeezed Fock states: A comparison with photon-subtracted counterparts arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies how adding photons to a two-mode squeezed Fock state affects its performance in Braunstein-Kimble quantum teleportation. The authors compare teleportation fidelity gains of the photon-added state with those of a photon-subtracted counterpart, accounting for the success probabilities of both operations. They find that photon subtraction performs better, with the advantage larger when success probability is included, and that symmetric (1,1) photon subtraction gives the best balance between fidelity and success probability.

entry.title: Performance of cat and GKP state generation using squeezed single-photon inputs
entry.summary: Performance analysis of cat and GKP breeding protocols with squeezed single-photon input arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper analyzes optical protocols that generate cat states and GKP grid states by homodyne breeding, using squeezed single photons as seeds. For a symmetric tree of seeds, the heralded resource state is shown to be close to the desired squeezed-cat resource, with closed-form even-cat fidelities and a rule for choosing seed squeezing. The resources are then applied to GKP breeding, with practical imperfections such as finite homodyne windows and photon loss also examined.

entry.title: Modelling NV⁻ spin-echo decoherence in nitrogen-rich diamond with a dynamical mean field
entry.summary: Dynamical-mean-field cluster-correlation expansion of NV⁻ spin-echo decoherence in a realistic substitutional-nitrogen bath arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper studies the Hahn-echo coherence time T₂ of NV⁻ centres in nitrogen-rich diamond. The authors replace the frozen mean field of surrounding P1 centres with a dynamical one, where pairs of P1 centres flip-flop while conserving total Sz, with rates from the dipolar Hamiltonian via kinetic Monte Carlo. At 30 mT this lowers T₂·[N] from 264 to 188 μs ppm, closer to experiment, without dark spins. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a dynamical mean field for CCE that replaces the frozen field, reporting parameter-free agreement with experiment at 10 and 30 mT and a remaining low-field discrepancy.

entry.title: Logarithmic Bias in Zero-Noise Extrapolation Under 1/f Noise
entry.summary: Logarithmic Bias of Zero-Noise Extrapolation under 1/f Noise arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper analyzes errors in zero-noise extrapolation when time-local Markovian noise and stationary finite-band 1/f noise are present together. The authors derive the response of complete multiqubit gate folding, which contains an r² ln r term, and show that ordinary polynomial extrapolation leaves a calculable bias from it. They propose response-matched extrapolation, including a log-domain implementation, that cancels this contribution, and give explicit bounds on the remaining errors.

entry.title: Barycentric programming: classical programs for universal quantum processors
entry.summary: Barycentric programming: Classical realization of programs for universal quantum processors arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper introduces barycentric programming, which stores the label of a unitary chosen randomly from a finite set, with probabilities set so that first-order approximation errors cancel in the averaged channel. As a result, the diamond-distance error scales quadratically with the discretization spacing. For ν-parameter unitary families forming a compact smooth manifold without boundary, the method achieves error ε using (ν/2)log₂(1/ε)+O(1) classical bits. The authors also prove a matching lower bound for arbitrary quantum programs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce barycentric programming, using randomized classical labels to cancel first-order errors and match the optimal leading-order program size, with a matching lower bound.

entry.title: Near-transform-limited pulse-like timing and narrowband spectra from sum-frequency generation with bright twin beams
entry.summary: Nearly Transform-Limited Pulse-Like Temporal and Narrowband Spectral Responses in Sum-Frequency Generation from Bright Twin Beams arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper simultaneously measures the timing and spectral behavior of the coherent part of bright twin beams using spectrally resolved, delay-dependent sum-frequency generation. The measured temporal correlation width is 0.138 ps, close to the 0.126 ps transform-limited value estimated from the twin-beam spectrum. The spectral correlation width is 0.176 rad/ps and is limited by spectrometer resolution. The time-frequency width product is 0.0243, far below the value of 1 expected for sum-frequency generation between two independent transform-limited Gaussian pulses.

entry.title: Quantum simulation of damped sound and elastic waves with absorbing boundaries and compact quantum circuits
entry.summary: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper simulates acoustic and elastic wave equations on a quantum computer while opening the domain with a graded sponge layer that damps waves near the outer edge. It uses Schrödingerisation to convert the non-unitary damped evolution into unitary evolutions via one auxiliary variable, deriving the full chain from partial differential equation to circuit in one, two and three dimensions. The authors report that damping all wave fields absorbs better than velocity-only damping, and that the damping step factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with classical solutions of the damped wave equations.

entry.title: Shallow circuits for loading multivariable functions into quantum states
entry.summary: Shallow data-loading circuits for multivariable functions arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper builds shallow quantum circuits, namely QROM, diagonal block-encoding, and state preparation oracles, for analytic functions on the D-dimensional hypercube [0,1]^D. Using n qubits and achieving error 2^{-Ω(n/D)}, the circuits reach depth O(√(n log₂(n)/D)) in the Clifford+T gate set. This requires 2^{O(√(nD log₂(n)))} ancilla qubits, and the depth is a near-quadratic reduction over known linear-depth methods.

entry.title: Probing non-adiabaticity in a quantum Otto cycle via quantum texture and imaginarity
entry.summary: Probing non-adiabaticity in a quantum Otto cycle through quantum texture and imaginarity arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies the non-adiabatic inner friction produced when a two-level quantum system is driven unitarily in finite time. The authors combine two resource-theoretic measures, quantum texture (rugosity) and imaginarity, into a combined witness that is non-negative and vanishes only for quasi-static driving. Applied to a finite-time quantum Otto refrigerator, it yields an exact closed-form relation between the coefficient of performance and these two quantities. The authors also report that local minima of the witness identify the operating regimes that maximize cooling performance.

entry.title: The Reference System Loophole: a paper on a gap in Extended Wigner's Friend theorems
entry.summary: The Reference System Loophole arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper argues that Extended Wigner's Friend theorems contain a previously unnoticed loophole, arising because measurement outcomes typically need a reference system to have meaning. The author shows how the loophole can preserve quantum mechanical predictions in the Local Friendliness theorem without denying Local Friendliness, and responds to some objections. The loophole is further claimed to apply to any Wigner's Friend experiment and to other Extended Wigner's Friend theorems.

entry.title: Angular-momentum pumping by moving charges via chirality
entry.summary: Chirality-Induced Angular-Momentum Pumping by Moving Charges arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes a mechanism for chirality-induced spin selectivity in which injected electron wave packets coherently emit chiral phonons. Competition between electronic absorption and phonon decay sets the fraction of electrons receiving the effect and its temperature dependence. The authors state that spin-orbit coupling is not renormalized but becomes effectively large because Coulomb correlations enhance the orbital and spin moments it couples.

entry.title: Lieb-Robinson bounds for Bose-Hubbard models via path expansions
entry.summary: Lieb-Robinson bounds for Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonians via path expansions arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies transport in Bose-Hubbard-type Hamiltonians. It gives shorter proofs of known bounds on particle transport and Lieb-Robinson velocity, using weighted extended particle number operators and a bosonic path-expansion method. The transport bounds are also extended to long-range hopping with power-law exponents above the lattice dimension.

entry.title: Quantum Temporal Marginal Problem: whether partial multi-time experiments can come from one quantum process
entry.summary: Quantum Temporal Marginal Problem arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper asks whether partial measurement results from a quantum process at selected times can come from one common underlying process. The authors formulate this process tensor marginal problem as a semidefinite feasibility test. They show that agreement on overlapping times is not sufficient, and quantify incompatibility by the mixing needed to restore compatibility. ★★★★ Notable: The authors formulate a process tensor marginal problem as an SDP, report that local consistency is insufficient, and show incompatibility equals a discrimination advantage.

entry.title: How quantum relationality relates to symmetry-based relationality
entry.summary: What is the connection between quantum relationality and symmetry-based relationality? arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper examines whether the relationality in quantum mechanics and the relationality in relativistic physics are fundamentally the same. It proposes that quantum states describe degrees of freedom that can be changed by a symmetry transformation, so they are relativized for the same reason as partial observables in general relativity. The author argues this hypothesis is consistent with existing empirical evidence and considers its implications for debates about the nature of quantum measurement.

entry.title: Inverse-designed silicon photonic beam splitters and how fabrication errors affect quantum protocol yield
entry.summary: From Fabrication Disorder to Quantum-Protocol Yield in Inverse-Designed Silicon Photonic Beam Splitters arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper uses adjoint-based inverse design to create compact 1×2 Y-splitters and 2×2 directional couplers for silicon spin-photon qubits at 1326 nm and 1482.44 nm. It evaluates fabrication variations such as etch bias, line-edge roughness, thickness, and refractive-index changes using 100-realization Monte Carlo simulations. The authors conclude that the tolerance of the target quantum protocol, rather than the device alone, sets the fabrication requirement for these beam splitters.

entry.title: Sound-wave interference reveals the symmetry of a quantum transition
entry.summary: Sound-wave interference reveals the symmetry of a quantum transition arXiv · Nov 2, 2026A single sound quantum emitted from two locations interferes with itself, and the fringe position shows whether the two sources emit with the same or opposite signs. Researchers measured single phonons emitted as a hole tunnels between two gallium arsenide quantum dots. They found the emission is mainly antisymmetric, with only a small symmetric part. This antisymmetric emission is predicted to strongly reduce phonon losses for qubits at their operating frequencies.

entry.title: Classical and quantum dynamics in projective Hilbert space, measurement, and classical emergence
entry.summary: Classical and Quantum Dynamics in State Space: Projective Hilbert Space, Measurement, and Classical Emergence arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes a geometric framework that takes projective Hilbert space as the primary state space, with classical configuration and phase spaces arising as submanifolds of localized quantum states. It extends the construction to Brownian motion, lifted to stochastic unitary evolution in projective Hilbert space. Applications discussed include measurement, classical emergence, the double-slit experiment, composite systems, and entangled states. The range and universality of this mechanism for realistic many-body measuring environments is stated as an open problem.

entry.title: Detection times are not local observables in quantum field theory
entry.summary: Detection times are not local observables in quantum field theory arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper shows that, under natural covariance and consistency requirements, observables describing detection times cannot be algebraically localized in any bounded spacetime region, even when the records themselves are localized. This challenges equating algebraic localization with the physical localization of measurements. The authors further argue that microcausality alone does not establish non-signalling for measurements in quantum field theory. ★★★★ Notable: The authors argue that detection-time observables cannot be algebraically localized in bounded regions, challenging the usual identification with physical localization of measurements.

entry.title: How interaction order sets the cost of sustaining quantum magic under noise
entry.summary: Interaction order sets the onset cost of steady-state quantum magic arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies the minimum resource cost of keeping a positive steady-state quantum magic in autonomous qubit networks subject to depolarization noise. It gives an optimal onset scaling of γ(γ/J)^{1/(k-1)} for local stabilizer replacement resets, with a leading coefficient of 1/(2√2) for two-body interactions. The converse bound uses hafnian stabilizer geometry together with a positive random-order forest expansion.

entry.title: Classical and quantum logics that each have several mutually non-equivalent, non-isomorphic models
entry.summary: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper concerns the finding that both quantum and classical logics have several models that are neither equivalent nor isomorphic to one another, a result that has been proved repeatedly in the literature. Some authors have recently criticized this result. The authors argue that these criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.

entry.title: A rule-based static analysis framework for quantum programs whose hardware constraints can be configured
entry.summary: Rule-based hardware-configurable static analysis for quantum programs arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper presents SHARP, a rule-based static analysis framework for OpenQASM that separates hardware-specific constraints from the validation engine. It ingests instruction set architecture descriptions as standalone data, so the core engine need not change when hardware is updated. The framework also uses an analysis-driven mechanism for multi-stage validation to simplify rule construction and improve extensibility.

entry.title: Quantum Path Finder: a new quantum algorithm design based on gauge dynamics in constraint space
entry.summary: Quantum Path Finder: Navigating Constraint Space via Non-Abelian Gauge Dynamics arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper introduces Quantum Path Finder (QPF), a quantum algorithm design paradigm that uses non-Abelian gauge dynamics within a constraint-protected degenerate manifold, with each Boolean variable encoded as a qutrit that includes an unassigned state. The authors illustrate the framework on unstructured search, complete 3-XORSAT, and satisfiable 3-SAT instances. They also outline a superconducting-qutrit implementation and discuss its conceptual relation to nondeterministic Turing machines.

entry.title: Phase-conjugate twin-wave coherent reception over 100 km of fiber using injection locking
entry.summary: Experimental demonstration of phase-conjugated twin-wave coherent reception over 100 km with injection locking assisted phase stabilization arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper experimentally demonstrates a coherent receiver that recovers 200-MBaud signals with modulation formats up to 256-QAM after 100 km of optical fiber. Optical injection locking regenerates the local oscillator from a reference sent through the link, and pilot-assisted optical feedback stabilizes the signal-to-local-oscillator phase so that phase-conjugated twin waves combine at one balanced photodetector. The reported signal-to-noise ratio exceeds the ideal single-mode homodyne standard quantum limit benchmark and conventional heterodyne results by about 3 dB and 6 dB, respectively. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report injection-locked phase-conjugated twin-wave reception over 100 km, with measured SNR above the single-mode SQL benchmark.

entry.title: Recovering quantum information from black-hole radiation beyond the mean emission yield
entry.summary: Quantum Recovery from Black-Hole Radiation Beyond the Emission Yield arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper asks how much information an outside observer can recover from radiation escaping a black hole. At a fixed mean radiation yield, it establishes a sharp recovery limit for single-excitation channels and realizes the qubit limit with an autonomous quantum-memory emitter. Unequal transmissions balance retained coherence against information in failed collection events. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish a recovery frontier at fixed mean radiation yield for single-excitation channels and realize its qubit limit with a quantum-memory emitter.

entry.title: Observable-algebra framework for quantum coherence in anyonic systems
entry.summary: An Observable-Algebra Approach to Quantum Coherence in Anyonic Systems arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper models physical restrictions on operations as subalgebras of accessible observables and splits quantum coherence into three nonnegative contributions. Applied to anyonic systems, it separates the effects of local-charge superselection from those of non-Abelian fusion rules. For pure anyonic states with vacuum total charge, the optimized total and correlated coherence are shown to equal the total and conventional relative-entropy entanglement, respectively.

entry.title: Quantum-enhanced estimation of two phases in spin-1 condensates
entry.summary: Quantum-enhanced multiphase estimation with spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies quantum-enhanced two-phase estimation in a spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensate, where spin-exchange collisions create a spin-nematic squeezed state. The state's quantum Fisher information matrix for the two phases has rank one, so the phases cannot be resolved independently. The authors show that a parameter-independent passive three-mode transformation removes this rank deficiency and enables joint estimation. Analytical results in the undepleted-pump regime are confirmed by exact diagonalization calculations.

entry.title: Reducing parameter sloppiness via intermediate controls in sequential spin interferometry
entry.summary: Mitigating sloppiness with intermediate controls in sequential multiparameter spin interferometry arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies sequential multiparameter quantum sensing in which two phases encoded through the same generator are locally indistinguishable. Using a collective-spin interferometer, the authors show that parameter-independent intermediate controls, including a transverse collective rotation and intermediate one-axis twisting (OAT), separate the effective generators. For fixed particle number and matched twisting resource, both marginal precision bounds are lower than those of a separated-OAT strategy. For intermediate OAT, optimizing an upper bound on the Holevo cost yields asymptotic N^-2 scaling.

entry.title: Suppressing decoherence in quantum dense coding
entry.summary: Decoherence suppression in quantum dense coding arXiv · Nov 1, 2026Quantum dense coding uses entanglement to send information beyond the limits of classical communication and is a key part of many quantum technologies. The paper studies non-Markovian decoherence dynamics in two types of dense coding protocols, one using discrete-variable and one using continuous-variable systems. It shows that a bound state forming in the energy spectrum of the whole system, including each subsystem and its local channel environment, restores the quantum advantage of dense coding despite decoherence.

entry.title: Bounds and Sufficient Conditions in Quantum Zeno Effect: Limits on state lifetime under repeated measurements and conditions for observing the inverse Zeno effect.
entry.summary: Bounds and sufficient conditions in quantum Zeno effect arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies how repeated measurements on a quantum system change its state lifetime as the interval between measurements varies, either shortening it (Zeno effect) or lengthening it (inverse Zeno effect). It derives upper and lower bounds on the optimized state lifetime, expressed through characteristic time scales in the survival probability P(T), and analyzes bounds on optimal measurement periods or rates along with sufficient conditions for the inverse Zeno effect. The analysis is extended to non-monotonic survival functions and illustrated numerically with optically trapped ultra-cold atoms.

entry.title: Access to measurement records and stability of error correction in continuous strategic codes
entry.summary: Access Resources and Stability of Error-Correction Capabilities in Continuous Strategic Codes arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies which parts of the measurement record a controller can use during recovery in continuous quantum error correction. It formulates continuous strategic codes using open continuous process tensors contracted with causal instruments and conditional recovery. For monitored stabilizer codes, it gives a criterion for merging records without loss and compares the costs of terminal labels and persistent memory. It also derives fidelity bounds and stability guarantees under model mismatch.

entry.title: From ghost SICs to SIC-POVMs: a Galois reduction of Zauner's conjecture
entry.summary: From Ghost SICs to SIC-POVMs: A Galois Reduction of Zauner's Conjecture arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper studies the existence of symmetric informationally complete POVMs (SIC-POVMs) in quantum information. The authors compute the isolated points of the complexified SIC variety for dimensions 4, 5 and 6, finding that exactly half are SICs. They show that passing from ghost SICs to genuine SICs is purely arithmetic and give a criterion based on a place law over a real quadratic field. Zauner's conjecture remains unproven in this work. ★★★★ Notable: The authors reduce ghost-to-SIC passage to arithmetic via a Galois place law, reporting computations for d=4,5,6 and proofs for several dimensions, with the Stark part unproved.

entry.title: Near-optimal learning of quantum many-body Hamiltonians from Gibbs and metastable thermal states
entry.summary: Near-Optimal Learning of Quantum Many-Body Systems from Gibbs and Thermal Metastable States via the Stationarity Test arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies learning a finite-range quantum Hamiltonian on an n-qubit lattice from copies of its Gibbs states at known inverse temperature β, or from its thermal metastable states. The proposed algorithm reduces the exponential dependence on β from e^{poly(β)} to e^{O(β)}, nearly optimal in the exponent. It builds on a stationarity-test framework and a temperature-independent frequency filter. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the temperature exponent in Hamiltonian learning sample complexity from poly(β) to linear in β, proving a Fisher-information coercivity bound.

entry.title: Superradiance from moiré exciton-biexciton condensates: entangled photon pairs versus supercurrent-driven emission
entry.summary: Superradiance fingerprints of moiré exciton-biexciton condensates: path-entangled biphoton vs. supercurrent-enabled one-photon channel arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This study examines the collective light emission of condensates formed by hybrid moiré excitons in twisted MoTe2 bilayers. Individual ground-state excitons have very long radiative lifetimes, and their emission becomes strong only once condensates form. The biexciton (molecular-type) condensate decays through superradiance that emits path-entangled biphotons, while the exciton (atomic-type) condensate is dark at rest and becomes superradiant when it carries a supercurrent.

entry.title: A paper on maximum purity, absolute separability, and spectral volumes of absolutely PPT quantum states
entry.summary: Purity maxima, absolute separability, and spectral volumes of absolutely PPT states arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) states and absolutely separable states in m⊗n quantum systems. Under specified dimension conditions, it determines their exact maximum purity and the unique maximizing ordered spectrum. These results disprove both cases of a maximum purity conjecture proposed by Ahiable, Kothakonda, and Winter. The paper also computes the purity maximum for completely absolutely separable states and the asymptotic order of the relative volumes of these sets under the uniform spectral measure. ★★★★ Notable: The authors determine exact maximum purity and unique maximizing spectra for APPT and absolutely separable states, disproving a conjecture with explicit boundary spectra in quantum entanglement theory

entry.title: Boson sampling is weak against photon loss
entry.summary: Boson sampling is fragile to loss arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper asks whether boson sampling experiments remain computationally hard when photons are lost. It shows that even a small, fixed, nonzero uniform loss rate lets a classical computer sample the output distribution efficiently on average. The method exploits the fact that loss suppresses many-photon correlations, so low correlation orders suffice for approximation. The authors conclude that a large photon count alone does not guarantee computational hardness. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that any fixed nonzero uniform photon loss allows average-case efficient classical sampling of boson sampling, with polynomial-time samplers for Fock and Gaussian variants.

entry.title: Diagnostic layer that checks whether quantum error-correction decoders preserve logical information
entry.summary: Logical-Class Diagnostic Layer for Stabilizer Codes and Decoders via Supercharge Structures arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper proposes a decoder-independent diagnostic layer for abelian Pauli stabilizer codes, aimed at fault-tolerant quantum computing. A nilpotent supercharge defined by an ancilla fermionic register has its degree-zero harmonic sector equal to the code space, and it is used to test whether a decoder's correction preserves every encoded input. The method also classifies residual errors modulo stabilizers into check violations, harmless stabilizer residuals, and syndrome-silent nontrivial logical actions.

entry.title: A bottom-up method linking scales to rebuild ground and excited states of extended molecular systems
entry.summary: Graph-Covariant Bottom-Up Scale-Bridging Reconstruction of Ground and Excited States of Extended Systems arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper proposes a hierarchical scale-bridging scheme, called encapsulation, for building first-principles electronic structure models of disordered extended molecular aggregates. Coarser-level variables parameterize finer-level operators through a recursive, graph-covariant structure. Applied to excitons, DFT and TDDFT results for monomers and dimers are combined via a many-body expansion to build aggregate-level operators, with a numerical demonstration on crystalline quaterthiophene.

entry.title: Theoretical estimation of nonlinear response functions and ultrafast spectroscopy of nitrogen-vacancy color centers
entry.summary: Theoretical estimation of nonlinear response function and ultrafast optical spectroscopy of nitrogen vacancy centers arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper extends the displaced harmonic oscillator model used to describe the ultrafast optical response of nitrogen-vacancy centers by including state-dependent oscillator modes with different frequencies. The authors show that the nonlinear response function gains a correction term that can be evaluated with operator algebra techniques. This change affects two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy, which resolves ultrafast correlated electron-vibrational dynamics.
